note: English overlay of myths.json, keyed by id. Translated only from the Japanese entries; original-text quotations are not translated. Names whose reading could not be confirmed are left in kanji with "(reading unconfirmed)".

tenchi.title: The Beginning of Heaven and Earth
tenchi.lead: When heaven and earth first opened, Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami appeared in the High Plain of Heaven (高天原), and then deities came into being one after another. The first five are grouped together as the "Separate Heavenly Deities" (別天神), and those from Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami through Izanagi-no-Kami and Izanami-no-Kami are grouped as the "Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods" (神世七代).

points.text: The first deity to appear in the Kojiki is Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami, who came into being in the High Plain of Heaven (高天原). Next Takamimusubi-no-Kami and Kamumusuhi-no-Kami came into being, and all three, as solitary deities (独神), hid their forms.

The five deities from Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami through Umashiashikabihikoji-no-Kami and 天之常立神 (reading unconfirmed) are regarded as the "Separate Heavenly Deities" (別天神), and they are written about separately from the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods that follow.

The deities from Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami through Izanagi-no-Kami and Izanami-no-Kami form the "Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods" (神世七代). The two solitary deities are each counted as one generation, and the ten male and female deities are counted two to a generation. At the end of these appear Izanagi-no-Kami and Izanami-no-Kami, who become the central figures of the birth of the land.

The main text of the Nihon Shoki (section 1) explains that heaven and earth separated out of a mixed state like a hen's egg, and gives Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto as the first deity. 天御中主尊 (reading unconfirmed), who corresponds to Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami, is only listed in variant account 4, introduced with "it is also said" (又曰), as a deity born in the High Plain of Heaven.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, the three deities Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami, Takamimusubi-no-Kami and Kamumusuhi-no-Kami are called the "Three Deities of Creation" (造化三神), based on wording in the preface of the Kojiki. Because Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami appears only in this opening passage and nothing it does is described, it is regarded as difficult to make clear what kind of deity it is.

According to the same database, many interpretations see the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods in the Kojiki as having the birth of Izanagi-no-Kami and Izanami-no-Kami as their goal, with the process leading up to it expressed step by step through the appearance of deities. Opinions differ on what that process represents (the formation of the land, the completion of the bodies of the male and female deities, and so on).

story.text: When heaven and earth first opened, the name of the deity who first came into being in the High Plain of Heaven (高天原) was Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami. Next Takamimusubi-no-Kami came into being, and next Kamumusuhi-no-Kami. These three all came into being as "solitary deities" (独神) without partners, and hid their forms. A small note in the original instructs that the character 天 in 高天原 be read "ama".

Next, when the land was still young, like floating oil, and drifting like a jellyfish (the original writes this part phonetically as 久羅下那州多陀用弊流), the deity that came into being from something that sprouted and grew up like a reed shoot was Umashiashikabihikoji-no-Kami. Next 天之常立神 (reading unconfirmed) came into being. These two also came into being as solitary deities and hid their forms. The five deities up to this point are called the "Separate Heavenly Deities" (別天神).

Then Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami came into being, and next Toyokumono-no-Kami, and these two also hid their forms as solitary deities. After that, deities came into being in male and female pairs: Uhijini-no-Kami and his younger sister Suhichini-no-Kami; Tsunogui-no-Kami and his younger sister Ikugui-no-Kami; Ōtonoji-no-Kami and his younger sister Ōtonobe-no-Kami; Omodaru-no-Kami and his younger sister Ayakashikone-no-Kami; and Izanagi-no-Kami and his younger sister Izanami-no-Kami.

The deities from Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami through Izanami-no-Kami are together called the "Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods" (神世七代). According to a small note, the two solitary deities are each counted as one generation, and the ten male and female deities that follow are counted two to a generation. In this way Izanagi-no-Kami and Izanami-no-Kami appear in the seventh and last generation, leading on to the next story, the birth of the land.

quotes.note: When heaven and earth first opened, the name of the deity who came into being in the High Plain of Heaven was Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami.
The name of the deity who came into being from something that sprouted and grew up like a reed shoot was (Umashiashikabihikoji-no-Kami).
The five deities up to this point are the "Separate Heavenly Deities" (別天神).
The deities from Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami through Izanami-no-Kami are together called the "Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods" (神世七代).

figures.name: 高天原 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The place where the first deities came into being when heaven and earth opened; the High Plain of Heaven. A small note instructs that 天 be read "ama", but the reading of the word as a whole cannot be confirmed from the original.

figures.name: Kamumusuhi-no-Kami (神産巢日神)
figures.role: The third solitary deity to come into being, after Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami and Takamimusubi-no-Kami.

figures.name: Umashiashikabihikoji-no-Kami (宇摩志阿斯訶備比古遅神)
figures.role: One of the Separate Heavenly Deities, who came into being, while the land was drifting, from something that sprouted and grew up like a reed shoot.

figures.name: Toyokumono-no-Kami (豊雲野神)
figures.role: A solitary deity who came into being after Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Kami; the second generation of the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods.

figures.name: Uhijini-no-Kami (宇比地迩神)
figures.role: The male deity of the first male-female pair to appear in the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods.

figures.name: Suhichini-no-Kami (須比智迩神)
figures.role: The female deity who appears paired with Uhijini-no-Kami (called his "younger sister" (妹) in the original).

figures.name: Tsunogui-no-Kami (角杙神)
figures.role: The male deity of one of the male-female pairs of the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods.

figures.name: Ikugui-no-Kami (活杙神)
figures.role: The female deity who appears paired with Tsunogui-no-Kami.

figures.name: Ōtonoji-no-Kami (意富斗能地神)
figures.role: The male deity of one of the male-female pairs of the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods.

figures.name: Ōtonobe-no-Kami (大斗乃弁神)
figures.role: The female deity who appears paired with Ōtonoji-no-Kami.

figures.name: Omodaru-no-Kami (於母陀流神)
figures.role: The male deity of one of the male-female pairs of the Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods.

figures.name: Ayakashikone-no-Kami (阿夜訶志古泥神)
figures.role: The female deity who appears paired with Omodaru-no-Kami.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 1, main text
compare.text: The main text of the Shoki describes the state before heaven and earth separated as a chaos like a hen's egg, and says that something like a reed shoot arose between heaven and earth and became a deity. The first deity is Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, followed by 国狭槌尊 (reading unconfirmed) and 豊斟渟尊 (reading unconfirmed); no deity corresponding to Ame-no-Minakanushi-no-Kami appears in the main text.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 1, variant account 4
compare.text: 天御中主尊, 高皇産霊尊 and 神皇産霊尊 (readings unconfirmed), who correspond to the first three deities of the Kojiki, are in the Shoki only listed in variant account 4, introduced with "it is also said" (又曰), as deities born in the High Plain of Heaven.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 3, main text (see also section 3, variant account 1)
compare.text: The main text of the Shoki also calls the deities from Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto through Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto the "Seven Generations of the Age of the Gods" (神世七代), but they consist of three male deities who came into being alone (section 1) and eight deities in four male-female pairs (section 2). 角樴尊 and 活樴尊 (readings unconfirmed), who correspond to Tsunogui-no-Kami and Ikugui-no-Kami in the Kojiki, appear not in the main text but in variant account 1 of section 3.

kuniumi.title: The Birth of the Land
kuniumi.lead: Receiving a command from the heavenly deities, Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto made Onogoro-shima with the heavenly spear 天沼矛 (reading unconfirmed), married there, and gave birth to the islands that became the land. Their first union did not go well because the female deity spoke first; after following the divination of the heavenly deities and starting over, the islands, beginning with the land 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed), were born.

points.text: The heavenly deities commanded Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto to put the land in order and make it firm, and gave them the spear 天沼矛 (reading unconfirmed). When the two stirred the sea with the spear from the bridge 天浮橋 (reading unconfirmed), the brine that dripped from the tip of the spear piled up and Onogoro-shima was formed.

At first, because Izanami-no-Mikoto spoke first, the child born, Hiruko, was set adrift in a reed boat, and Awashima was not counted among their children either. Through the heavenly deities' divination (太占) it became clear that this was "because the woman spoke first", and they started over with Izanagi-no-Mikoto speaking first.

After starting over, eight islands were born, from Awaji-no-Ho-no-Sawake-no-shima to Ōyamato-toyoakizu-shima, and because these were born first, the name 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed) arose. Then six more islands, including 吉備児嶋 (reading unconfirmed), were also born.

In the main text of the Nihon Shoki (section 4) there is no command from the heavenly deities; the two deities themselves say, "Surely there must be a land below," and probe with the spear. When the female deity calls out first, the male deity rebukes her on the spot and they start over, and there is no consultation with the heavenly deities or divination. The first island born is also different, 大日本豊秋津洲 (reading unconfirmed), and 淡路洲 (reading unconfirmed) is called the "afterbirth" (胞).

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, "Onogoro" is interpreted as meaning "to congeal by itself", and the name is said to indicate that it was an island that formed naturally, not one born from the marriage of the two deities.

According to the same database, views on the name "Hiruko" are divided between a view that it means, as the characters suggest, a child like a leech, and a view that the characters are phonetic substitutes for "日子" (child of the sun). In addition, since the statement that the child "could not stand on its legs even at three years old" is found only in section 5 of the Nihon Shoki, doubts have also been raised about applying it to the Hiruko of the Kojiki.

story.text: The heavenly deities commanded the two deities Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto to put this drifting land in order and make it firm, and gave them the spear 天沼矛 (reading unconfirmed). The two stood on the bridge 天浮橋 (reading unconfirmed), lowered the spear, stirred the sea water until it made a sound, and drew it up. The brine that dripped from the tip of the spear piled up and became an island. This is Onogoro-shima.

The two descended to that island and set up the pillar 天之御柱 (reading unconfirmed) and the hall 八尋殿 (reading unconfirmed). When Izanagi-no-Mikoto asked how her body was formed, Izanami-no-Mikoto answered that "there is one place that did not grow together", and Izanagi-no-Mikoto said that he had "one place that grew in excess". Izanagi-no-Mikoto proposed that they join these and give birth to the land, and Izanami-no-Mikoto agreed. The two decided to go around 天之御柱 and meet, Izanami-no-Mikoto going around from the right and Izanagi-no-Mikoto from the left.

When they met, Izanami-no-Mikoto first said, "Ah, what a fine young man!" and afterwards Izanagi-no-Mikoto said, "Ah, what a fine young woman!" (the original writes these words phonetically). Izanagi-no-Mikoto told her that "it was not good that the woman spoke first", but they united anyway, and the child born was Hiruko. This child was put in a reed boat and set adrift, and Awashima, born next, was not counted among their children either.

The two consulted together, went up to the heavenly deities and asked for instructions. The heavenly deities divined by the method 太占 (reading unconfirmed) and told them that it had not been good because the woman spoke first, so they should go down again and say the words over. The two descended again and went around 天之御柱 as before, and this time Izanagi-no-Mikoto called out first and Izanami-no-Mikoto afterwards.

In this way the two united and gave birth to eight islands: Awaji-no-Ho-no-Sawake-no-shima, Iyo-no-Futana-no-shima, 隠伎之三子嶋 (reading unconfirmed), Tsukushi-no-shima, 伊伎嶋 (reading unconfirmed), 津嶋 (reading unconfirmed), Sado-no-shima and Ōyamato-toyoakizu-shima. Iyo-no-Futana-no-shima and Tsukushi-no-shima each have one body and four faces, and each face has a name: 愛比売, 飯依比古, Ōgetsu-hime and 建依別; and 白日別, 豊日別, 建日向日豊久士比泥別 and 建日別 (readings unconfirmed). Because these eight islands were born first, the land is called 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed).

After that, on their way back, they further gave birth to 吉備児嶋, 小豆嶋, 大嶋, 女嶋, 知訶嶋 and 両児嶋 (readings unconfirmed). These islands also each have another name: 建日方別, 大野手比売, 大多麻流別, 天一根, 天之忍男 and 天両屋 (readings unconfirmed). A small note counts the islands from 吉備児嶋 to 天両屋 together as six islands.

quotes.note: Put this drifting land in order and make it firm (the command of the heavenly deities).
The brine that dripped from the tip of the spear piled up and became an island. This is Onogoro-shima.
It is not good that the woman spoke first (the words of Izanagi-no-Mikoto).
Because these eight islands were born first, the land is called 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 天沼矛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The spear the heavenly deities gave to the two deities. With it they stirred the sea, and Onogoro-shima was formed.

figures.name: 天浮橋 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The place where the two deities stood and lowered the spear.

figures.name: Onogoro-shima (淤能碁吕嶋)
figures.role: The island formed when the brine that dripped from the tip of the spear piled up. The place where the two deities descended and married.

figures.name: 天之御柱 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The pillar set up on Onogoro-shima. The two deities went around it, met, and married.

figures.name: 八尋殿 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The hall set up on Onogoro-shima together with the pillar 天之御柱.

figures.name: Hiruko (水蛭子)
figures.role: The child born from the first union. It was put in a reed boat and set adrift.

figures.name: Awashima (淡嶋)
figures.role: The island born after Hiruko. It was not counted among the children.

figures.name: Awaji-no-Ho-no-Sawake-no-shima (淡道之穗之狹別嶋)
figures.role: The first island born after the deities started over.

figures.name: Iyo-no-Futana-no-shima (伊豫之二名嶋)
figures.role: An island with one body and four faces. Each face has the name of a province.

figures.name: Tsukushi-no-shima (筑紫嶋)
figures.role: Like Iyo-no-Futana-no-shima, an island with one body and four faces.

figures.name: Sado-no-shima (佐度嶋)
figures.role: An island born as one of the islands of 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Ōyamato-toyoakizu-shima (大倭豊秋津嶋)
figures.role: The eighth island born among the islands of 大八嶋国 (reading unconfirmed). Its other name is 天御虚空豊秋津根別 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Ōgetsu-hime (大宜都比賣)
figures.role: The name of one of the four faces of Iyo-no-Futana-no-shima, that of the province 粟国 (reading unconfirmed). It is regarded as a different deity with the same name as Ōgetsu-hime-no-Kami (大宜都比売神), who is born in the birth of the deities (database of deity names).

figures.name: 大八嶋國 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The collective name for the eight islands that were born first.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 4, main text
compare.text: In the main text of the Shoki there is no command from the heavenly deities; Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) and Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) consult together on their own on the bridge 天浮橋 (reading unconfirmed), probe with the spear 天之瓊矛 (reading unconfirmed), and obtain Onogoro-shima (磤馭慮島). When they go around the pillar and the female deity calls out first, the male deity rebukes her on the spot and they start over; there is no consultation with the heavenly deities and no divination (太占).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 4, main text
compare.text: The main text of the Shoki calls 淡路洲 (reading unconfirmed) the "afterbirth" (胞) and first gives birth to 大日本豊秋津洲 (reading unconfirmed). 蛭児 and 淡洲 (readings unconfirmed) do not appear in the birth of the land in the main text, and islands such as 対馬 and 壱岐 (readings unconfirmed) are said to have formed from congealed sea foam.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 4, variant account 1
compare.text: Variant account 1 is close to the Kojiki: the command of the heavenly deities, setting 蛭児 (reading unconfirmed) adrift in a reed boat, not counting 淡洲 (reading unconfirmed) among the children, and starting over through divination (太占). However, when they first go around the pillar the female deity goes left and the male deity right, and when they start over they also switch directions. In the Kojiki the female deity goes right and the male deity left from the start, and they go around the same way when they start over.

kamiumi.title: The Birth of the Deities and the Fire Deity
kamiumi.lead: Having finished giving birth to the land, Izanagi-no-Mikoto and Izanami-no-Mikoto gave birth one after another to deities of the sea, wind, trees, mountains, fields and so on, but Izanami-no-Mikoto was burned and died because she gave birth to the fire deity. When the grieving Izanagi-no-Mikoto cut down the fire deity Kagutsuchi-no-Kami (迦具土神), still more deities came into being from its blood and body.

points.text: Because Izanami-no-Mikoto gave birth to the fire deity 火之夜芸速男神 (reading unconfirmed; also called 火之迦具土神), her private parts were burned, she fell ill, and at last she departed this world (神避). Even during her illness, deities such as 金山毗古神 (reading unconfirmed), 波迩夜須毗売神 (reading unconfirmed), Mitsuhanome-no-Kami and Wakumusubi-no-Kami came into being from her vomit, feces and urine.

The grieving Izanagi-no-Mikoto cut off the head of his child Kagutsuchi-no-Kami with a ten-fist sword (十拳剣). From the blood on the sword came eight deities, including 建御雷之男神 (reading unconfirmed), and from the body of Kagutsuchi-no-Kami came eight mountain deities (山津見神), such as Masakayamatsumi-no-Kami. The name of that sword is Ame-no-Ohabari (also 伊都之尾羽張, reading unconfirmed).

In the birth of the deities, the deity of the sea (大綿津見神, reading unconfirmed), the deities of the river mouths (Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami and Hayaakitsu-hime-no-Kami), the deity of the wind (志那都比古神, reading unconfirmed), the deity of trees (Kukunochi-no-Kami), the deity of mountains (Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami) and the deity of fields (Kayano-hime-no-Kami) are born with their roles named in the original. Further, the two river-mouth deities divide the rivers and the sea between them, and the two deities of mountains and fields divide the mountains and the fields between them, and give birth to further deities.

From the tears of Izanagi-no-Mikoto came Nakisawame-no-Kami, and Izanami-no-Kami was buried on 比婆之山 (reading unconfirmed), on the border of Izumo Province and 伯伎国 (reading unconfirmed). A small note counts what the two deities gave birth to together before Izanami-no-Kami departed as fourteen islands and thirty-five deities, and states that Onogoro-shima is not an island they gave birth to.

In the main text of the Nihon Shoki (section 5) there is neither the birth of the fire deity nor the death of Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊); after the deities of mountains, rivers, grasses and trees, the two deities give birth to the sun deity, the moon deity, 蛭児 (reading unconfirmed) and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔嗚尊). The fire deity (Kagutsuchi, 軻遇突智) and the death of Izanami-no-Mikoto are transmitted in the variant accounts, and variant account 6 tells a story close to that of the Kojiki.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, 建御雷之男神 (reading unconfirmed) is a deity who came into being from the blood at the base of the sword that cut down the fire deity, and is placed as the child of 伊都之尾羽張 (reading unconfirmed), the deity of that sword. The element "futsu" in its other names 建布都神 and 豊布都神 (readings unconfirmed) is regarded as a word related to swords, and it has been pointed out that this deity has a strong character as a deity of swords. This deity later becomes an envoy in the scene of the transfer of the land (国譲り).

story.text: Having finished giving birth to the land, the two deities went on to give birth to deities. First Ōkotooshio-no-Kami was born, and next Iwatsuchibiko-no-Kami, 石巣比売神, 大戸日別神, 天之吹男神 (readings unconfirmed), Ōyabiko-no-Kami and 風木津別之忍男神 (reading unconfirmed) were born. Further, 大綿津見神 (reading unconfirmed) was born as the deity of the sea, and Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami and his younger sister Hayaakitsu-hime-no-Kami as the deities of the river mouths.

Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami and Hayaakitsu-hime-no-Kami divided the rivers and the sea between them and gave birth to further deities. These are eight deities: 沫那芸神, 沫那美神, 頬那芸神, 頬那美神, 天之水分神, 国之水分神, 天之久比奢母智神 and 国之久比奢母智神 (readings unconfirmed). A small note sums these up as "eight deities in all" (并八神).

Next the two deities gave birth to the deity of the wind, 志那都比古神 (reading unconfirmed), the deity of trees, Kukunochi-no-Kami, the deity of mountains, Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami, and the deity of fields, Kayano-hime-no-Kami (also called 野椎神, reading unconfirmed). Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami and 野椎神 divided the mountains and the fields between them and gave birth to eight deities: 天之狭土神, 国之狭土神, 天之狭霧神, 国之狭霧神, 天之闇戸神, 国之闇戸神, 大戸惑子神 and 大戸惑女神 (readings unconfirmed). Then the two deities gave birth to 鳥之石楠船神 (reading unconfirmed; also called Ame-no-Torifune-no-Kami) and Ōgetsu-hime-no-Kami.

The next child they gave birth to was 火之夜芸速男神 (reading unconfirmed), also called 火之炫毗古神 and 火之迦具土神 (readings unconfirmed). Because she gave birth to this child, Izanami-no-Mikoto had her private parts burned and fell ill. At that time 金山毗古神 and 金山毗売神 came into being from her vomit, 波迩夜須毗古神 and 波迩夜須毗売神 from her feces (readings unconfirmed), and Mitsuhanome-no-Kami and Wakumusubi-no-Kami from her urine; the child of Wakumusubi-no-Kami is called 豊宇気毗売神 (reading unconfirmed). Thus, because she gave birth to the fire deity, Izanami-no-Kami at last departed this world (神避, that is, died).

Izanagi-no-Mikoto lamented, "I have exchanged my beloved wife for a single child," and wept, crawling about by Izanami-no-Mikoto's pillow and by her feet. The deity who came into being from his tears is Nakisawame-no-Kami, who dwells at the foot of the trees at 畝尾 on 香山 (readings unconfirmed). The dead Izanami-no-Kami was buried on 比婆之山 (reading unconfirmed), on the border of Izumo Province and 伯伎国 (reading unconfirmed).

Izanagi-no-Mikoto drew the ten-fist sword (十拳剣) he wore at his waist and cut off the head of his child Kagutsuchi-no-Kami. The blood on the tip of the sword spattered onto the rocks 湯津石村 (reading unconfirmed), and Iwasaku-no-Kami, 根拆神 and 石筒之男神 (readings unconfirmed) came into being; from the blood at the base of the sword came Mikahayahi-no-Kami, 樋速日神 (reading unconfirmed) and 建御雷之男神 (reading unconfirmed; also called 建布都神 and 豊布都神). From the blood that gathered on the hilt of the sword and leaked out between his fingers came Kuraokami-no-Kami and 闇御津羽神 (reading unconfirmed). A small note sums these up as eight deities born through the sword.

Deities also came into being from the body of the slain Kagutsuchi-no-Kami. These are eight deities: Masakayamatsumi-no-Kami at the head, 淤縢山津見神 at the chest, 奥山津見神 at the belly, 闇山津見神 at the private parts, 志芸山津見神 at the left hand, 羽山津見神 at the right hand, 原山津見神 at the left foot and 戸山津見神 at the right foot (readings unconfirmed). The name of the sword that cut down Kagutsuchi-no-Kami is Ame-no-Ohabari, also called 伊都之尾羽張 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: Because she gave birth to the fire deity, Izanami-no-Kami at last died.
My beloved wife! Have I exchanged you for a single child? (the lament of Izanagi-no-Mikoto)
He drew the ten-fist sword he wore at his waist and cut off the head of his child Kagutsuchi-no-Kami.
The name of the sword that cut down Kagutsuchi-no-Kami is Ame-no-Ohabari.

figures.name: Ōkotooshio-no-Kami (大事忍男神)
figures.role: The first deity born in the birth of the deities, after the birth of the land.

figures.name: Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami (速秋津日子神)
figures.role: A deity of the river mouths. Dividing the rivers and the sea with his younger sister Hayaakitsu-hime-no-Kami, he gives birth to eight deities.

figures.name: Hayaakitsu-hime-no-Kami (速秋津比賣神)
figures.role: A deity of the river mouths. She gives birth to deities as a pair with Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami.

figures.name: Kukunochi-no-Kami (久々能智神)
figures.role: A deity born as the deity of trees.

figures.name: Kayano-hime-no-Kami (鹿屋野比賣神)
figures.role: The deity of fields. Her other name is 野椎神 (reading unconfirmed); dividing the mountains and the fields with Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami, she gives birth to eight deities.

figures.name: Mitsuhanome-no-Kami (弥都波能賣神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the urine of Izanami-no-Mikoto as she lay ill.

figures.name: Nakisawame-no-Kami (泣澤女神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the tears of Izanagi-no-Mikoto as he lamented the death of Izanami-no-Mikoto. She dwells at the foot of the trees at 畝尾 on 香山 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: Iwasaku-no-Kami (石拆神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being when the blood on the tip of the sword spattered onto the rocks 湯津石村 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Mikahayahi-no-Kami (甕速日神)
figures.role: The first of the three deities who came into being from the blood at the base of the sword.

figures.name: Kuraokami-no-Kami (闇淤加美神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the blood that gathered on the hilt of the sword and leaked out between the fingers.

figures.name: Masakayamatsumi-no-Kami (正鹿山津見神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the head of the slain Kagutsuchi-no-Kami.

figures.name: 十拳釼 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The ten-fist sword Izanagi-no-Mikoto wore at his waist. With it he cut off the head of Kagutsuchi-no-Kami.

figures.name: Ame-no-Ohabari (天之尾羽張)
figures.role: The name of the sword that cut down Kagutsuchi-no-Kami. Its other name is 伊都之尾羽張 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 比婆之山 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A mountain on the border of Izumo Province and 伯伎国 (reading unconfirmed). Izanami-no-Kami was buried there.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, main text
compare.text: In the main text of the Shoki, after giving birth to the sea, the rivers, the mountains, the ancestor of trees and the ancestor of grasses, the two deities consult about giving birth to a "ruler of all under heaven" and give birth to the sun deity (Ōhirume-no-Muchi, 大日孁貴), the moon deity, 蛭児 (reading unconfirmed) and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔嗚尊). The birth of the fire deity and the death of Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) are not written in the main text.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 6
compare.text: Variant account 6 is close to the Kojiki: Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) dies with the birth of Kagutsuchi (軻遇突智), Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) laments that he has exchanged his wife for a single child, and 啼沢女命 (reading unconfirmed) comes into being from his tears. However, the details differ: for example, Kagutsuchi is cut into three pieces, and deities such as Mikahayahi-no-Kami (甕速日神), 熯速日神 (reading unconfirmed) and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami (武甕槌神) come into being from the blood dripping from the sword.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 5
compare.text: On the place where Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) was buried, variant account 5 gives the village 有馬村 (reading unconfirmed) in Kumano, Kii Province, which differs from the Kojiki's "比婆之山 on the border of Izumo Province and 伯伎国".

yomi.title: The Land of Yomi
yomi.lead: Izanagi-no-Mikoto goes to bring back his wife Izanami-no-Mikoto, who has gone to the Land of Yomi (黄泉国), but he breaks her plea "do not look at me", sees her utterly changed form, is pursued, and flees back. After blocking the slope 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed) with a rock and exchanging words of parting, Izanagi-no-Mikoto goes to perform purification (禊) to cleanse himself of defilement, and twelve deities are born from the belongings he throws off.

points.text: Izanagi-no-Mikoto broke Izanami-no-Mikoto's request, "Do not look at me while I talk with the deities of Yomi (黄泉神)," lit a light and looked, and so came to be pursued by Izanami-no-Mikoto, who had been put to shame.

After 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed) was blocked with a rock that would take a thousand men to pull (千引石), Izanami-no-Mikoto said, "I will kill a thousand people a day," and Izanagi-no-Mikoto replied, "I will build fifteen hundred birthing huts a day." The Kojiki tells this as the origin of why, each day, a thousand people surely die and fifteen hundred are born.

Izanagi-no-Mikoto drove off his pursuers with three peaches from the foot of the slope, gave those peaches the name Ōkamuzumi-no-Mikoto, and commanded them to help the people of the Central Land of Reed Plains (葦原中国) too when they suffer.

In variant account 9 of section 5 of the Nihon Shoki as well, Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) throws peaches and drives off the thunder deities, and this is explained as the origin of using peaches to ward off demons. On the other hand, peaches do not appear in variant account 6, which records a different tradition, that he urinated on a great tree and caused a great river to arise.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, regarding the rock that blocked the slope (Chigaeshi-no-Ōkami, 道反之大神), there is a view that sees 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed) as the boundary between this world and the world of the dead, and reads in the rock the character of a boundary deity, like the roadside deities (道祖神) or barrier deities (塞の神) that hold back the intrusion of evil things.

According to the same database, the way of escape in which hair ornaments and combs are thrown and the pursuers are held up by the food that springs from them is regarded as fitting the pattern of the "magic flight", which is found widely around the world. However, the final peaches drive off the pursuers by the power of the peaches themselves, and the influence of the idea, of Chinese origin, that peaches drive away demons has been pointed out.

story.text: Wishing to see his wife Izanami-no-Mikoto, Izanagi-no-Mikoto followed her to the Land of Yomi (黄泉国). When Izanami-no-Mikoto met him at the door of the palace, Izanagi-no-Mikoto called to her, "The land that the two of us have been making is not yet finished, so I want you to come back." Izanami-no-Mikoto replied, "I wish you had come sooner. I have already eaten the food of Yomi (黄泉戸喫)." Even so, she asked, "Since it is an awesome thing that you have come, I wish to return. I will go and talk for a while with the deities of Yomi, so please do not look at me in the meantime," and went back into the depths of the palace. Having been made to wait so very long, Izanagi-no-Mikoto broke off one of the thick end teeth of the comb he wore in the left loop of his hair (mizura), lit it, went in and looked. Maggots were swarming over Izanami-no-Mikoto's body, and on her head, chest, belly, private parts, left and right hands and left and right feet, eight thunder deities in all had arisen.

Izanagi-no-Mikoto was afraid and fled. Izanami-no-Mikoto said, "You have put me to shame," and had Yomotsu-shikome pursue him. When Izanagi-no-Mikoto threw away his black hair ornament, wild grapes (蒲子) sprang up, and he escaped while the pursuers picked them up and ate them; when he broke off the comb from the right loop of his hair and threw it, bamboo shoots sprang up, and while they pulled them up and ate them he escaped again. Next Izanami-no-Mikoto had the eight thunder deities pursue him with an army of fifteen hundred from Yomi, and Izanagi-no-Mikoto kept fleeing, swinging his ten-fist sword (十拳剣) behind him.

When he reached the foot of 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed), Izanagi-no-Mikoto took three peaches that were there, waited, and struck at them, and the pursuers all fled back. Izanagi-no-Mikoto told the peaches, "Just as you have helped me, help the people living in the Central Land of Reed Plains (葦原中国) too when they meet with hardship and are troubled," and gave them the name Ōkamuzumi-no-Mikoto. Last of all, Izanami-no-Mikoto herself came in pursuit. Izanagi-no-Mikoto blocked 黄泉比良坂 with a rock that would take a thousand men to pull (千引石), and the two deities faced each other across the rock and exchanged words of parting. When Izanami-no-Mikoto said, "If you do this, I will strangle a thousand of the people of your land each day," Izanagi-no-Mikoto answered, "Then I will build fifteen hundred birthing huts each day." The Kojiki records that this is why, each day, a thousand people surely die and fifteen hundred are born.

Because of this, Izanami-no-Mikoto is called 黄泉津大神 (reading unconfirmed), and because she caught up with Izanagi-no-Mikoto she is also called 道敷大神 (reading unconfirmed). The rock that blocked the slope is called Chigaeshi-no-Ōkami (道反大神), and also 塞坐黄泉戸大神 (reading unconfirmed). 黄泉比良坂 is said to be what is now 伊賦夜坂 (reading unconfirmed) in Izumo Province.

Izanagi-no-Ōkami said, "I have been to a terribly defiled land. So I will perform purification (禊) to cleanse my body," and went to 阿波岐原 at 小門 of 橘 in 日向 in 竺紫 (readings unconfirmed) and performed purification and exorcism (禊祓). From the staff, sash, skirt, robe, trousers and headdress, and the left and right armbands that he threw away there, twelve deities were born, from 衝立船戸神 (reading unconfirmed) to Hetsukaibera-no-Kami. The Kojiki explains these as deities born from his taking off the things he had been wearing.

quotes.note: My beloved wife, the land that you and I have been making is not yet finished. So I want you to come back.
I will go and talk for a while with the deities of Yomi, so please do not look at me in the meantime.
(Then) I will build fifteen hundred birthing huts a day.
This is why, each day, a thousand people surely die, and each day fifteen hundred people are surely born.

figures.name: Yomotsu-kami (黃泉神)
figures.role: The deities of the Land of Yomi, with whom Izanami-no-Mikoto said she would go to consult about whether she might return.

figures.name: Yakusa-no-Ikazuchi-no-Kami (八雷神)
figures.role: The thunder deities that had arisen at eight places on Izanami-no-Mikoto's body. Given an army of fifteen hundred from Yomi, they pursued Izanagi-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: Yomotsu-shikome (豫母都志許賣)
figures.role: The first pursuer Izanami-no-Mikoto sent. Izanagi-no-Mikoto escaped from her while she was eating what sprang up from the hair ornament and comb he threw.

figures.name: Ōkamuzumi-no-Mikoto (意富加牟豆美命)
figures.role: The name Izanagi-no-Mikoto gave to the peaches that drove off the pursuers at the foot of 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Chigaeshi-no-Ōkami (道反大神)
figures.role: The name given to the rock, which would take a thousand men to pull, that blocked 黄泉比良坂 (reading unconfirmed). It is also called 塞坐黄泉戸大神 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Michi-no-Nagachiha-no-Kami (道之長乳齒神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the sash he threw away before the purification.

figures.name: 時置師神 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the skirt he threw away (this is the spelling in this edited text; the database of deity names uses as its headword the spelling of another manuscript, 時量師神, and states that there are various views on the reading, so no reading is given).

figures.name: Wazurai-no-Ushi-no-Kami (和豆良比能宇斯能神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the robe he threw away.

figures.name: Chimata-no-Kami (道俣神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the trousers he threw away.

figures.name: Akigui-no-Ushi-no-Kami (飽咋之宇斯能神)
figures.role: A deity who came into being from the headdress he threw away.

figures.name: Okizakaru-no-Kami (奧疎神)
figures.role: The first of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the left hand that he threw away.

figures.name: Okitsunagisabiko-no-Kami (奧津那藝佐毗古神)
figures.role: The second of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the left hand.

figures.name: Okitsukaibera-no-Kami (奧津甲斐弁羅神)
figures.role: The third of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the left hand.

figures.name: Hezakaru-no-Kami (邊疎神)
figures.role: The first of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the right hand that he threw away.

figures.name: Hetsunagisabiko-no-Kami (邊津那藝佐毗古神)
figures.role: The second of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the right hand.

figures.name: Hetsukaibera-no-Kami (邊津甲斐弁羅神)
figures.role: The third of the three deities who came into being from the armband of the right hand.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 6
compare.text: In the scene where, in the Kojiki, Izanami-no-Mikoto says she "has already eaten the food of Yomi (黄泉戸喫)", Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) in variant account 6 says, "I have already eaten food cooked in the hearth of the Spring (泉)." The pursuers are also given as eight Yomotsu-shikome (泉津醜女).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 6
compare.text: The Kojiki says that 黄泉比良坂 is 伊賦夜坂 in Izumo Province (readings unconfirmed), but variant account 6 states that 泉津平坂 (reading unconfirmed) is perhaps not a place that exists somewhere else, but refers to the time when one's breath fails as one faces death.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 9
compare.text: In variant account 9, Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) hides beneath a great peach tree, throws its fruit at the thunder deities and makes them retreat, and this is explained as the origin of using peaches to ward off demons. Where the eight thunder deities are located also differs from the Kojiki: for example, the back and the buttocks, and a mountain thunder and a field thunder, appear.

misogi.title: Purification and the Three Noble Children
misogi.lead: When Izanagi-no-Mikoto rinsed himself in the middle shallows of a river, deities arising from defilement, deities that set right that misfortune, and deities of the sea were born one after another, and finally, from his left eye, right eye and nose, the Three Noble Children (三貴子) were born: Amaterasu-Ōmikami, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto and Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Izanagi-no-Mikoto entrusted to the three deities, respectively, the High Plain of Heaven (高天原), the realm of the night (夜の食国) and the sea plain, but Susanoo-no-Mikoto did not obey, kept weeping and wailing, and was driven out.

points.text: When Izanagi-no-Mikoto washed his left eye in the purification (禊), Amaterasu-Ōmikami was born; with his right eye, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; and with his nose, Susanoo-no-Mikoto (written 建速須佐之男命). Izanagi-no-Mikoto rejoiced greatly, saying, "At the last I have obtained three noble children." These are the "Three Noble Children" (三貴子).

Izanagi-no-Mikoto gave Amaterasu-Ōmikami the jewels of his necklace (Mikuratana-no-Kami) and entrusted her with ruling the High Plain of Heaven (高天原); he entrusted Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto with ruling the realm of the night (夜の食国), and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (written 建速須佐之男命) with ruling the sea plain.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto did not rule the sea plain but wept and wailed, "I want to go to 根の堅洲国 (reading unconfirmed), the land of my mother," withering the mountains and drying up the rivers and seas, and so the angry Izanagi-no-Mikoto drove him out of this land.

In the purification, first Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami and Ōmagatsuhi-no-Kami were born from the defilement of the Land of Yomi (黄泉国), and then Kamunaobi-no-Kami, Ōnaobi-no-Kami and Izunome, who set that misfortune right, were born. From the bottom, middle and top of the water, deities of the 綿津見神 and 筒之男命 (readings unconfirmed) were born, three of each.

In the main text of section 5 of the Nihon Shoki, the sun deity (Ōhirume-no-Muchi, 大日孁貴), the moon deity and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔嗚尊) are regarded as children born together by the two deities Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) and Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊); the story in which the three deities are born when he washes his eyes and nose in the purification is found in variant account 6.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, the Magatsuhi deities (禍津日神) and the Naobi deities (直毘神) have paired names. Views on the Magatsuhi deities are divided, among others, between a view that sees them as deities that cause misfortune and a view that sees them as deities that censure wrongdoing and make it be corrected, and the debate continues.

story.text: Izanagi-no-Mikoto said, "The upper shallows are fast-flowing and the lower shallows are weak-flowing," and he dived into the middle shallows and rinsed himself. At that time, first Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami and Ōmagatsuhi-no-Kami were born. These two deities are recorded as having been born from the filth from when he went to a land full of defilement. Next, in order to set that misfortune right, three deities were born: Kamunaobi-no-Kami, Ōnaobi-no-Kami and Izunome.

When he rinsed himself at the bottom of the water, 底津綿津見神 and 底筒之男命 were born; when he rinsed himself in the middle, 中津綿津見神 and 中筒之男命; and when he rinsed himself at the top of the water, 上津綿津見神 and 上筒之男命 (readings unconfirmed). The three 綿津見神 (reading unconfirmed) are deities worshipped as ancestral deities by the 阿曇連 (reading unconfirmed) and others, and the 阿曇連 and others are said to be descendants of Utsushihikanasaku-no-Mikoto, a child of the 綿津見神. The three 筒之男命 (reading unconfirmed) are recorded as being the three great deities of 墨江 (墨江の三前の大神; reading unconfirmed).

Next, when he washed his left eye, Amaterasu-Ōmikami was born; when he washed his right eye, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; and when he washed his nose, Susanoo-no-Mikoto (written 建速須佐之男命). The fourteen deities from Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami to Susanoo-no-Mikoto (written 速須佐之男命) are regarded as deities born from his rinsing himself. Izanagi-no-Mikoto rejoiced greatly and said, "I have been giving birth to child after child, and at the last I have obtained three noble children." Then he shook the jewel cord he wore around his neck, gave it to Amaterasu-Ōmikami, and entrusted her, saying, "You shall rule the High Plain of Heaven (高天原)." The jewels of this necklace are called Mikuratana-no-Kami. Next he entrusted Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto with ruling the realm of the night (夜の食国), and Susanoo-no-Mikoto with ruling the sea plain.

But Susanoo-no-Mikoto (written 速須佐之男命) alone did not rule the land entrusted to him, and kept weeping and wailing until his long beard reached down to his chest. His weeping was such that it turned green mountains into withered mountains and wept the waters of the rivers and seas completely dry. Because of this, the voices of evil deities filled everything like flies, and every kind of calamity arose.

When Izanagi-no-Mikoto asked the reason, Susanoo-no-Mikoto answered, "I am weeping because I want to go to 根の堅洲国 (reading unconfirmed), the land of my late mother." Izanagi-no-Mikoto was furious, said, "Then you shall not live in this land," and drove him out. The Kojiki records that Izanagi-no-Ōkami is enshrined at 多賀 in 淡海 (readings unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The upper shallows flow too fast and the lower shallows flow too weakly (so he rinses himself in the middle shallows).
I have been giving birth to child after child, and at the end of my giving birth I have obtained three noble children.
You shall rule the High Plain of Heaven (words to Amaterasu-Ōmikami).
I am weeping because I want to go to the land of my late mother, 根の堅洲国 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami (八十禍津日神)
figures.role: One of the two deities born, when he rinsed himself in the middle shallows, from the filth from when he went to a land full of defilement.

figures.name: Ōmagatsuhi-no-Kami (大禍津日神)
figures.role: A deity born from the filth together with Yasomagatsuhi-no-Kami.

figures.name: Kamunaobi-no-Kami (神直毗神)
figures.role: The first of the three deities born in order to set the misfortune right.

figures.name: Ōnaobi-no-Kami (大直毗神)
figures.role: The second of the three deities born in order to set the misfortune right.

figures.name: Izunome (伊豆能賣)
figures.role: The third of the three deities born in order to set the misfortune right.

figures.name: Utsushihikanasaku-no-Mikoto (宇都志日金拆命)
figures.role: A child of the 綿津見神 (reading unconfirmed); the 阿曇連 (reading unconfirmed) and others are recorded as his descendants.

figures.name: Mikuratana-no-Kami (御倉板擧之神)
figures.role: The name of the necklace jewels that Izanagi-no-Mikoto gave to Amaterasu-Ōmikami (a reading note says that 板擧 is read "tana").

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, main text
compare.text: In the main text of section 5, Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊) and Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊弉冉尊) consult together, saying, "Let us give birth to one who will be ruler of all under heaven," and together give birth to the sun deity, whom they name Ōhirume-no-Muchi (大日孁貴); it does not say that she was born from the purification.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 6
compare.text: Even in variant account 6, where the three deities are born from the purification, the places entrusted to them differ from the Kojiki: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto (月読尊) is commanded to rule the eightfold layers of the tides of the blue sea plain, and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔嗚尊) to rule all under heaven.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 5, variant account 6
compare.text: In variant account 6, the misfortune deity born when he rinses himself in the middle shallows is only one, 八十枉津日神 (reading unconfirmed), the deities that set it right are two, 神直日神 and 大直日神 (readings unconfirmed), and no deity corresponding to Izunome appears.

ukei.title: The Pledge at the Heavenly River 天の安の河 (reading unconfirmed)
ukei.lead: When the banished Susanoo-no-Mikoto came up to the High Plain of Heaven (高天原) to bid farewell, Amaterasu-Ōmikami suspected that he had come to seize her land and met him armed. The two deities made a pledge (誓約, ukei) across the heavenly river 天の安の河 (reading unconfirmed) and each gave birth to children; Susanoo-no-Mikoto claimed victory, saying that the purity of his heart had been shown, and committed acts of violence in the High Plain of Heaven.

points.text: Amaterasu-Ōmikami suspected that Susanoo-no-Mikoto had come to seize her land and met him armed; so that Susanoo-no-Mikoto could show the purity of his heart, the two deities made a pledge (誓約) across the river 天安河 (reading unconfirmed) and each gave birth to children from the other's belongings.

Amaterasu-Ōmikami gave birth to three female deities from Susanoo-no-Mikoto's ten-fist sword (十拳剣), and Susanoo-no-Mikoto gave birth to five male deities, including Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto, from Amaterasu-Ōmikami's jewels; Amaterasu-Ōmikami decided, according to whose belongings they came from, that the male deities were her children and the female deities were Susanoo-no-Mikoto's children.

In the Kojiki, no agreement is written before the pledge about which children being born would mean a pure heart. Susanoo-no-Mikoto declared on his own, "I have won," on the grounds that the children born were girls.

Emboldened by his victory, Susanoo-no-Mikoto ravaged the rice fields and defiled the palace, and further dropped a piebald horse into the sacred weaving hall (忌服屋), causing the death of the heavenly weaving maiden (天衣織女). Immediately after this, the story of the "Heavenly Rock-Cave Door" (天の岩屋戸) begins.

In the main text of section 6 of the Nihon Shoki, before the pledge Susanoo-no-Mikoto sets out the condition, "If girls are born, my heart is impure; if boys are born, my heart is pure," so the way victory and defeat are decided differs from the Kojiki.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, the names of the three female deities, and which goddess dwells in which shrine, disagree among the various traditions of the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki, and the shrine's own tradition at Munakata Taisha (宗像大社) is said to worship them in an order that follows the main text of the Nihon Shoki.

story.text: Susanoo-no-Mikoto said, "Then I will take my leave after informing Amaterasu-Ōmikami," and went up to heaven. At that time the mountains and rivers all shook, and the whole land trembled. Amaterasu-Ōmikami heard this and was alarmed, and said, "Susanoo-no-Mikoto's coming up is not from a good heart. He means to seize my land."

Amaterasu-Ōmikami undid her hair and retied it in loops (mizura), and on the left and right loops, on her hair ornament, and on her left and right hands she wound strings of many long curved jewels (勾玉). On her back she bore a quiver holding a thousand arrows, at her side she fastened a quiver holding five hundred, on her arm she put a bamboo arm guard, and she brandished her bow. Then she stamped into the hard ground up to her thighs, kicking it about like powdery snow, gave a valiant war cry, and demanded, "Why have you come up?"

Susanoo-no-Mikoto answered, "I have no evil heart. When I was asked why I was weeping and said that I wanted to go to my mother's land, I was driven out, so I have only come to bid you farewell." Amaterasu-Ōmikami asked, "Then how can I know that your heart is pure and bright?" Susanoo-no-Mikoto answered, "Let us each make a pledge and give birth to children."

The two deities made the pledge across the river 天安河 (reading unconfirmed). First Amaterasu-Ōmikami took Susanoo-no-Mikoto's ten-fist sword, broke it into three, rinsed it in the well 天の真名井 (reading unconfirmed) and chewed it up, and from the mist of her breath as she blew it out three deities were born: 多紀理毘売命 (also called 奥津島比売命), 市寸島比売命 (also called 狭依毘売命) and 多岐都比売命 (readings unconfirmed). Susanoo-no-Mikoto took the jewels wound on Amaterasu-Ōmikami's left hair loop and did the same, and 正勝吾勝勝速日 (reading unconfirmed) Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto was born. Further, from the jewels of the right hair loop, the hair ornament, the left hand and the right hand were born Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto, Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto, Ikutsuhikone-no-Mikoto and Kumanokusubi-no-Mikoto.

Amaterasu-Ōmikami divided them and decided, "The five boys born afterwards came into being from my belongings, so they are my children. The three girls born first came into being from your belongings, so they are your children." The three female deities are said to dwell in the 奥津宮, 中津宮 and 辺津宮 shrines of 胸形, and to be the three great deities worshipped by the 胸形君 (readings unconfirmed) and others. It is also recorded that Takehiratori-no-Mikoto, the child of Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto (written 天菩比命), is the ancestor of the Izumo provincial chieftains (出雲国造) and others, and that Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto is the ancestor of the 凡川内国造 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto said, "Because my heart is pure and bright, the children I gave birth to were graceful girls. So I have won." Then, emboldened by his victory, he broke down the ridges between Amaterasu-Ōmikami's rice fields and filled in the ditches, and scattered excrement in the palace where she partook of the great harvest offering (大嘗). Even so, Amaterasu-Ōmikami did not rebuke him but put a better face on it, saying, "What looks like excrement must be what he vomited when drunk. Breaking the ridges and filling the ditches must be because he begrudged the land being wasted."

But Susanoo-no-Mikoto's violence did not stop and grew even worse. When Amaterasu-Ōmikami was having garments for the deities woven in the sacred weaving hall (忌服屋), Susanoo-no-Mikoto made a hole in its roof and dropped in a heavenly piebald horse that he had flayed backwards. The heavenly weaving maiden (天衣織女) who was weaving at the loom was startled, struck her private parts with the shuttle, and died.

quotes.note: Susanoo-no-Mikoto's coming up is surely not from a good heart. He means only to seize my land.
Then how am I to know that your heart is pure and bright?
The five boys born afterwards came into being from my belongings, so they are my children.
Because my heart is pure and bright, the children I gave birth to were graceful girls. So naturally I have won.

figures.name: Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto (天之菩卑能命)
figures.role: The second male deity, born from the jewels on Amaterasu-Ōmikami's right hair loop. His child Takehiratori-no-Mikoto is regarded as the ancestor of the Izumo provincial chieftains (出雲国造) and others.

figures.name: Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto (天津日子根命)
figures.role: The third male deity, born from the jewels of the hair ornament. He is regarded as the ancestor of many clans, such as the 凡川内国造 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Ikutsuhikone-no-Mikoto (活津日子根命)
figures.role: The fourth male deity, born from the jewels of the left hand.

figures.name: Kumanokusubi-no-Mikoto (熊野久須毗命)
figures.role: The fifth male deity, born from the jewels of the right hand.

figures.name: Takehiratori-no-Mikoto (建比良鳥命)
figures.role: The child of Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto (written 天菩比命). He is recorded as the ancestor of seven clans, including the Izumo provincial chieftains (出雲国造) and the 无邪志国造 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 十拳釼 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The ten-fist sword Susanoo-no-Mikoto wore. Amaterasu-Ōmikami broke it into three and chewed it up, and three female deities were born.

figures.name: 八尺勾璁之五百津之美須麻流之珠 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The jewels Amaterasu-Ōmikami wound on her hair loops, hair ornament and both hands. Susanoo-no-Mikoto gave birth to five male deities from them.

figures.name: 天衣織女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The woman who was weaving garments for the deities in the sacred weaving hall (忌服屋). Startled by the piebald horse dropped in, she struck her private parts with the shuttle and died.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 6, main text
compare.text: In the main text of section 6, before the pledge Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔鳴尊) sets out the condition, "If those born are girls, you may regard my heart as impure; if boys, as pure." In the Kojiki there is no prior agreement, and Susanoo-no-Mikoto claims victory on the grounds that girls were born.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 6, variant account 1
compare.text: In variant account 1 there is no exchange of belongings: the sun deity chews the ten-span, nine-span and eight-span swords (十握剣, 九握剣, 八握剣) that she herself wears and gives birth to the three goddesses, and Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔鳴尊) gives birth to the five male deities from the jewels hung around his own neck.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 7, main text
compare.text: In the Kojiki the one who dies while weaving at the loom is the heavenly weaving maiden (天衣織女), but in the main text of section 7 it is Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照大神) herself, weaving garments for the deities, who is startled and injures herself with the shuttle, and because of this she shuts herself in the heavenly rock cave (天石窟).

iwayado.title: The Heavenly Rock-Cave Door
iwayado.lead: When Amaterasu-Ōmikami shut herself inside the Heavenly Rock-Cave Door (天石屋戸), both the High Plain of Heaven (高天原) and the Central Land of Reed Plains (葦原中国) grew dark, and all kinds of calamities arose. The myriad deities (八百万の神々) consulted together, gathered the implements for a ritual, lured Amaterasu-Ōmikami out with the dance of Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto and the laughter of the deities, and restored light to the world.

points.text: When Amaterasu-Ōmikami closed the Heavenly Rock-Cave Door (天石屋戸) and shut herself in, both the High Plain of Heaven (高天原) and the Central Land of Reed Plains (葦原中国) became pitch dark, night went on and on, and every kind of calamity arose.

The myriad deities gathered at the riverbed of the heavenly river 天の安の河 (reading unconfirmed), had Omoikane-no-Kami (思金神) draw up a plan, had 伊斯許理度売命 (reading unconfirmed) make a mirror and Tamanooya-no-Mikoto make strings of curved jewels (勾玉), hung them on the branches of a sakaki tree (榊), and prayed.

When Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto became possessed by the deity and danced before the door, the myriad deities laughed; they showed the mirror to Amaterasu-Ōmikami, who had opened the door wondering at this, and Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Kami took her by the hand and drew her out, and so light returned to the world.

In the main text of section 7 of the Nihon Shoki as well, the sequence is shared: the plan of Omoikane-no-Kami (思兼神), the prayers of Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto (天児屋命) and Futodama-no-Mikoto (太玉命), the dance of Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto (天鈿女命), and the drawing out by 手力雄神 (reading unconfirmed). However, there is no scene in which a mirror is held out and shown to Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照大神); instead, Amaterasu-Ōmikami herself opens the door a crack and peeps out, and 手力雄神 draws her out.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, regarding Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto's act of baring her breasts and private parts, there are views such as that it aimed at the revival of nature through laughter, and that it relates to rites for pacifying the spirit (鎮魂), and in each of them its meaning as a rite for the revival of the sun deity is given great weight.

The same database explains that the name of Omoikane-no-Kami (思金神) is often interpreted, from the Nihon Shoki spelling 思兼神, as a deity combining many kinds of thought, and that it is regarded as a deity that appears throughout the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki as an adviser to Amaterasu-Ōmikami.

story.text: Seeing the violence of Susanoo-no-Mikoto told in the previous story, Amaterasu-Ōmikami was afraid, closed the Heavenly Rock-Cave Door (天石屋戸), and shut herself inside. Then the High Plain of Heaven (高天原) became completely dark, the Central Land of Reed Plains (葦原中国) too was wrapped in darkness, and there was nothing but night. The voices of many deities filled the surroundings like swarms of flies, and every kind of calamity arose.

So the myriad deities (八百万の神々) gathered at the riverbed of the heavenly river 天の安の河 (reading unconfirmed) and had Omoikane-no-Kami (思金神), a child of Takamimusubi-no-Kami, devise a plan. The deities gathered the long-crying birds of 常世 (reading unconfirmed) and made them cry, took hard stones from the upper reaches of the heavenly river 天の安の河 and iron from the heavenly metal mountain (天の金山), and sought out the smith Amatsumara. They had 伊斯許理度売命 (reading unconfirmed) make a mirror, and Tamanooya-no-Mikoto make strings of long curved jewels (八尺の勾玉).

Further, they summoned Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto and Futodama-no-Mikoto (布刀玉命) and had them divine, pulling out the shoulder bone of a stag from 天香山 (reading unconfirmed) and using wood of the 波波迦 (reading unconfirmed) tree from 天香山. They dug up a sakaki tree (榊) of 天香山 by the roots, and hung the strings of jewels on its upper branches, the mirror 八尺鏡 (reading unconfirmed) on its middle branches, and white and blue cloth on its lower branches. Futodama-no-Mikoto held this up as an offering (御幣), Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto recited a ritual prayer (祝詞), and Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Kami stood hidden beside the door.

Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto hung the 日影 vine (reading unconfirmed) of 天香山 across her shoulders as a sash, made a hair ornament of the 真拆 vine (reading unconfirmed), and held bundled bamboo-grass leaves in her hand. Then she turned a tub (汙氣) upside down in front of the Heavenly Rock-Cave Door and stamped on it until it resounded, became possessed by the deity, bared her breasts, and pushed the cord of her skirt down to her private parts. At this the myriad deities all laughed at once, so that the High Plain of Heaven rang with it.

Amaterasu-Ōmikami wondered at this, opened the door a crack, and asked, "Since I have shut myself away, the world should be dark, so why is Ame-no-Uzume dancing so merrily and why are the deities laughing?" Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto answered, "We are rejoicing and laughing because there is a deity here more noble than you." Meanwhile Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto and Futodama-no-Mikoto held out the mirror and showed it to her, and Amaterasu-Ōmikami, wondering more and more, came out from the door little by little.

At that moment Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Kami, who had been standing hidden, took Amaterasu-Ōmikami by the hand and drew her out, and Futodama-no-Mikoto at once stretched a rope (尻久米縄, reading unconfirmed) across behind her and said, "You cannot go back inside beyond this." When Amaterasu-Ōmikami thus came out, both the High Plain of Heaven and the Central Land of Reed Plains became bright and illuminated of themselves.

quotes.note: She closed the Heavenly Rock-Cave Door and shut herself away inside.
The myriad deities all laughed at once, so that the High Plain of Heaven rang with it.
(Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto's answer) We are rejoicing, laughing and making merry because there is a deity here more noble than you.
Both the High Plain of Heaven and the Central Land of Reed Plains became bright and illuminated of themselves.

figures.name: Amatsumara (天津麻羅)
figures.role: The smith (a metalworking craftsman) who was sought out to make the mirror.

figures.name: 常世長鳴鳥 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The birds that were gathered and made to cry in order to call Amaterasu-Ōmikami out.

figures.name: 八尺勾𤥼之五百津之御須麻流之珠 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The strings of curved jewels made by Tamanooya-no-Mikoto, hung on the upper branches of the sakaki tree.

figures.name: 八尺鏡 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The mirror made by 伊斯許理度売命 (reading unconfirmed), hung on the middle branches of the sakaki tree and held out to Amaterasu-Ōmikami (a reading note in the original says that 八尺 is read 八阿多).

figures.name: 天香山之五百津真賢木 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The sakaki tree dug up by the roots from 天香山 (reading unconfirmed), hung with jewels, mirror and cloth, and used in the ritual.

figures.name: 尻久米繩 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The rope that Futodama-no-Mikoto stretched across behind Amaterasu-Ōmikami so that she could not go back into the rock cave.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 7, main text
compare.text: The main text of the Nihon Shoki says that Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto (天鈿女命) held in her hand a spear wound with reeds (茅) and performed skillfully as an entertainer (俳優, wazaogi) in front of the door of the heavenly rock cave (天石窟); this is depicted differently from the Kojiki's figure who becomes possessed with bamboo-grass leaves in her hand.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 7, main text
compare.text: In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照大神), hearing of Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto's (天鈿女命) behavior, opens the door a crack with her own hand and peeps out, and at that point 手力雄神 (reading unconfirmed) draws her out; there is no scene, as in the Kojiki, in which a mirror is held out and shown to her.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 7, variant account 2
compare.text: Variant account 2 records that when the mirror was put into the rock cave it touched the door and received a small scratch, which still remains today, and states that this mirror is the great deity enshrined at Ise. This statement is not in the Kojiki.

orochi.title: The Banishment of Susanoo-no-Mikoto and Yamata-no-Orochi
orochi.lead: Driven out of the High Plain of Heaven (高天原), Susanoo-no-Mikoto met, in the upper reaches of the river 肥の河 (reading unconfirmed) in Izumo, an old couple weeping because their daughter was about to be eaten by Yamata-no-Orochi, and he made the great serpent drunk with sake and slew it. He presented to Amaterasu-Ōmikami the sword Kusanagi-no-Tachi, which came out of the serpent's tail, built a palace at 須賀 (reading unconfirmed) and lived there with 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed), and from their descendants Ōkuninushi-no-Kami (大国主神) was born.

points.text: Susanoo-no-Mikoto made Yamata-no-Orochi, which had eight heads and eight tails, drink strong sake, and when it was drunk and asleep he cut it to death with his ten-fist sword (十拳剣) and saved 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed).

When he cut the middle tail of the serpent, the blade of his sword was chipped, and a great sword was found inside the tail. Susanoo-no-Mikoto presented it to Amaterasu-Ōmikami, and this is Kusanagi-no-Tachi.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto was made by the myriad deities to bear a penalty, had his hair (鬢) and nails cut, and was banished from the High Plain of Heaven. Also, from the body of the slain 大気都比売神 (reading unconfirmed) arose silkworms, rice, foxtail millet, adzuki beans, wheat and soybeans, and 神産巣日御祖命 (reading unconfirmed) made these into seeds.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto built a palace at 須賀 (reading unconfirmed), composed a song, and made Ashinazuchi the head of the palace. From the descendants of Susanoo-no-Mikoto and 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed) is born Ōkuninushi-no-Kami, who has five names.

In the main text of section 8 of the Nihon Shoki, the child born to Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔鳴尊) and 奇稲田姫 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as Ōanamuchi (大己貴神), which differs from the genealogy of the Kojiki, which places Ōkuninushi-no-Kami as a descendant many generations later.

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, besides being classified as a tale of the "Perseus-Andromeda type", in which a monster is defeated and a sacrificial maiden is saved, the story of Yamata-no-Orochi has also been viewed as a representation of the floods of the river 肥の河 (today's 斐伊川; readings unconfirmed), and there are views that connect the sword that came out of the tail with ironmaking and smithing in Izumo, among others.

story.text: The myriad deities (八百万の神々) consulted together, made Susanoo-no-Mikoto bear a great many articles of atonement (千位置戸), cut his hair (鬢) and the nails of his hands and feet, and drove him out of the High Plain of Heaven (高天原). Also, when food was asked of 大気都比売神 (reading unconfirmed), she took various delicious things from her nose, mouth and buttocks, cooked them and offered them. Susanoo-no-Mikoto, peeping at what she was doing, thought that she was defiling the food before offering it, and killed 大気都比売神.

From the body of the slain 大気都比売神 (reading unconfirmed) arose silkworms at the head, rice seeds in the two eyes, foxtail millet in the two ears, adzuki beans in the nose, wheat in the private parts, and soybeans in the buttocks. 神産巣日御祖命 (reading unconfirmed) had these taken and made them into seeds.

The banished Susanoo-no-Mikoto descended to a place called 鳥髪 (reading unconfirmed) in the upper reaches of the river 肥の河 (reading unconfirmed) in Izumo Province. Chopsticks came floating down the river, so, thinking there were people upstream, he went up and found an aged couple weeping with a girl between them. The husband named himself Ashinazuchi, an earthly deity (国つ神) and a child of Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami; the wife was Tenazuchi, and the daughter 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed). They said that the couple had originally had eight daughters, but the Yamata-no-Orochi of 高志 (reading unconfirmed) came every year and ate them, and now the time had come again this year, so they were weeping.

As for the appearance of Yamata-no-Orochi, its eyes were red like akakagachi (according to a small note, what is now called 酸醤), and it had eight heads and eight tails on one body. Moss, cypress and cedar (檜, 榅) grew on its body, its length stretched across eight valleys and eight peaks, and its belly was always inflamed with blood.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto announced that he was the younger brother of Amaterasu-Ōmikami (the original has 伊呂勢) and had just now come down from heaven, and so it was settled that he would receive the daughter. Susanoo-no-Mikoto turned 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed) into a many-toothed comb (湯津爪櫛) and stuck it in his own hair, had the couple brew sake made strong by repeated brewing, had them build a fence around and make eight gates, and had them place at each gate a platform (佐受岐) and a sake vat, and wait. Yamata-no-Orochi came, put each of its eight heads into a sake vat and drank the sake, became drunk and fell asleep on the spot.

Susanoo-no-Mikoto drew the ten-fist sword at his waist and cut the serpent to pieces, and the river 肥の河 flowed as blood. When he cut the middle tail the blade of his sword was chipped, so, wondering at this, he split the tail open with the tip of his sword and found the great sword 都牟羽の大刀 (reading unconfirmed) inside. Susanoo-no-Mikoto thought this an extraordinary thing and presented it to Amaterasu-Ōmikami. This is Kusanagi-no-Tachi.

After that, Susanoo-no-Mikoto looked in Izumo Province for land on which to build a palace, and when he arrived at 須賀 (reading unconfirmed) he said, "Having come here, my heart is refreshed (sugasugashii)," and built a palace. Since clouds rose up at that time, he composed a song (the song is written in the original in man'yōgana, one character per syllable). Ashinazuchi was appointed head of this palace and given the name 稲田宮主須賀之八耳神 (reading unconfirmed). Generation after generation followed from Yashimajinumi-no-Kami, the child of Susanoo-no-Mikoto and 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed), and Ōkuninushi-no-Kami was born as the child of Ame-no-Fuyukinu-no-Kami and Sashikuni-wakahime. Ōkuninushi-no-Kami also has the other names 大穴牟遅神, 葦原色許男神, 八千矛神 and 宇都志国玉神 (readings unconfirmed), five names in all.

quotes.note: (From the slain 大気都比売神, reading unconfirmed) silkworms arose at the head, and rice seeds in the two eyes.
Yamata-no-Orochi truly came, just as had been said, put one of its heads into each sake vat, and drank the sake.
This is Kusanagi-no-Tachi.
Having come to this land, my heart is refreshed. (Told as the origin of the place name 須賀, reading unconfirmed.)

figures.name: Yamata-no-Orochi (八俣遠吕智)
figures.role: A great serpent with eight heads and eight tails that came every year and ate the daughters of Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi; it is slain by Susanoo-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: Ashinazuchi (足名椎)
figures.role: An earthly deity (国つ神), a child of Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami, and the father of 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed). He is later made head of the palace at 須賀 (reading unconfirmed) and given the name 稲田宮主須賀之八耳神 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Tenazuchi (手名椎)
figures.role: The wife of Ashinazuchi and the mother of 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 神産巢日御祖命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The deity who had the things that arose from the body of the slain 大気都比売神 (reading unconfirmed) taken and made them into seeds (the database of deity names treats this as another name of Kamumusuhi-no-Kami).

figures.name: Kusanagi-no-Tachi (草那藝之大刀)
figures.role: The great sword that came out of the tail of Yamata-no-Orochi, which Susanoo-no-Mikoto presented to Amaterasu-Ōmikami.

figures.name: 十拳釼 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The sword with which Susanoo-no-Mikoto cut Yamata-no-Orochi; its blade was chipped when it struck the great sword inside the tail.

figures.name: Yashimajinumi-no-Kami (八嶋士奴美神)
figures.role: The child of Susanoo-no-Mikoto and 櫛名田比売 (reading unconfirmed), and the first deity in the genealogy leading to Ōkuninushi-no-Kami.

figures.name: Kamuōichi-hime (神大市比賣)
figures.role: A daughter of Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami, who with Susanoo-no-Mikoto gave birth to Ōtoshi-no-Kami and Ukanomitama-no-Kami.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 8, main text
compare.text: In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, Ōanamuchi (大己貴神) is regarded as born directly as the child of Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔鳴尊) and 奇稲田姫 (reading unconfirmed); it does not have a genealogy like that of the Kojiki, which reaches Ōkuninushi-no-Kami after many generations from Yashimajinumi-no-Kami.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 8, main text (variant account in a small note)
compare.text: The variant account in a small note attached to the main text of the Nihon Shoki gives the original name of the sword 草薙剣 (reading unconfirmed) as 天叢雲剣 (reading unconfirmed), explains that this was perhaps because there were always clouds above the serpent, and relates that it was renamed 草薙剣 in the time of Prince Yamato Takeru (日本武皇子). This explanation is not in this section of the Kojiki.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 8, variant account 2
compare.text: In variant account 2, the setting and plot differ from the Kojiki: for example, the place where Susanoo-no-Mikoto (素戔鳴尊) descended is given as the upper reaches of the river 可愛 in 安芸国 (readings unconfirmed), and the one about to be swallowed by the serpent is a child yet to be born.

inaba.title: The Hare (素兎) of 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed)
inaba.lead: 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed; Ōkuninushi-no-Kami), taken along as an attendant by the Eighty Deities (八十神) as they set out for 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed) to seek the hand of Yakami-hime, healed by the correct method a hare that was suffering after being skinned. The hare declared that it would be 大穴牟遅神 who would win Yakami-hime, and, just so, Yakami-hime rejected the Eighty Deities and answered that she would marry 大穴牟遅神.

points.text: 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed; Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) taught the hare, which was suffering after being skinned, to wash its body in the water of the river mouth and roll about on kama-no-hana (蒲黄) spread out beneath it, and the hare's body was healed as it had been before.

The hare tricked the wani (和迩) by proposing a contest to compare the numbers of their kin, and crossed from 淤岐嶋 (reading unconfirmed) to the cape of 気多 (reading unconfirmed) by stepping on their backs; but just before it finished crossing it spoke of having tricked them, so it was caught by the wani and had its fur stripped off.
The Eighty Deities (八十神) taught the injured hare a wrong method of healing, "Bathe in sea water and expose yourself to the wind," and made the hare's wounds even worse.

The healed hare declared that 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed) would win Yakami-hime, and, just so, Yakami-hime rejected the Eighty Deities and answered that she would marry 大穴牟遅神. The Kojiki begins telling this story as the reason why the Eighty Deities all yielded the land to Ōkuninushi-no-Kami.

In the books on the Age of the Gods of the Nihon Shoki (Books 1 and 2), no passage corresponding to the story of the hare of 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed), the Eighty Deities and Yakami-hime could be confirmed. The Nihon Shoki records the same deity mainly under the name "Ōanamuchi" (大己貴).

According to the Kokugakuin University database of deity names, there is a view that the 素 in "素菟" means white and a view that it means naked. Also, because stories in which a land animal tricks water animals in order to cross the water are found widely abroad too, there is a view that it was originally an independent animal story unrelated to Ōkuninushi-no-Kami.

story.text: Ōkuninushi-no-Kami had many brothers, called the Eighty Deities (八十神), but they all came to yield the land to Ōkuninushi-no-Kami. The reason is as follows. The Eighty Deities each wished to marry Yakami-hime of 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed), and set out together for 稲羽; at that time they made 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed; Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) carry a bag on his back and took him along as an attendant.

When the party arrived at the cape (前, a headland) of 気多 (reading unconfirmed), a naked hare was lying collapsed there. The Eighty Deities told the hare, "You should bathe in the salt water of the sea, expose yourself to the wind, and lie on the ridge of a high mountain." When the hare did as it was told, as the salt dried the skin of its body was split by the blowing wind, and it lay weeping, suffering from the pain.

When 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed), who came last, asked the reason, the hare told the following story. The hare, which was on 淤岐嶋 (reading unconfirmed), had wanted to cross over here but had no means of doing so, so it tricked the wani (和迩) of the sea, proposing: "Let us compare which of our kin are more numerous. Bring all your companions and lie in a row from the island to the cape of 気多. I will step on you and count as I cross." When the wani lined up, it crossed by stepping on them and counting, but just as it was about to step down onto land it said, "You have been tricked," and was caught by the wani at the very end, which stripped off all its clothing (its fur). On top of that, because it followed the teaching of the Eighty Deities, its whole body was injured.

So 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed) taught it: "Go at once to this river mouth, wash your body in its water, take the kama-no-hana (蒲黄) of the river mouth, spread it out and roll about on it, and you will surely be healed so that your skin is as it was." When the hare did as it was told, its body became as it had been before. This is the hare (素菟) of 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed), and it is now called Usagi-gami (菟神).

The hare told 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed), "The Eighty Deities will never win Yakami-hime. Even though you carry the bag, it is you who will win her." And indeed Yakami-hime answered the Eighty Deities, "I will not listen to what you say. I will marry 大穴牟遅神."

quotes.note: (The teaching of 大穴牟遅神, reading unconfirmed) Wash your body with the water, and at once take the kama-no-hana of that river mouth (and spread it out).
This is the hare (素菟) of 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed), and it is now called Usagi-gami.
(The hare's words) Even though you carry the bag, it is you who will win (Yakami-hime).
(Yakami-hime's answer) I will not listen to what you say. I will marry 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Usagi-gami (菟神)
figures.role: The hare that tricked the wani, had its fur stripped off, and was healed by 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed). The original also calls it "the hare of 稻羽" (稻羽之素菟) and says that it is now called Usagi-gami.

figures.name: 八十神 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The many brothers of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami (the Eighty Deities), who set out for 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed) to seek the hand of Yakami-hime and taught the hare a wrong method of healing.

figures.name: Yakami-hime (八上比賣)
figures.role: A goddess who lived in 稲羽 (reading unconfirmed); she rejected the proposals of the Eighty Deities and answered that she would marry 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Wani (和迩)
figures.role: Sea creatures that were tricked by the hare into lying in a row in the sea, and at the end caught the hare and stripped off its fur.

figures.name: Kama-no-hana (蒲黃)
figures.role: What 大穴牟遅神 (reading unconfirmed) taught the hare to spread out and roll about on; with it the hare's body was restored.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 1, section 8, variant account 6
compare.text: In Books 1 and 2 of the Nihon Shoki, no passage corresponding to the story of the hare of 稲羽, the Eighty Deities and Yakami-hime could be confirmed.
