This sword had been sent down by Takemikazuchi-no-Kami at the command of Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照大神) and 高木神 (reading unconfirmed), and a note in the original text records its names, such as Futsunomitama (布都御魂), and that it is at Isonokami Shrine (石上神宮).

Beyond Kumano, Yatagarasu (八咫烏), sent from heaven by 高木大神 (reading unconfirmed), served as guide. In Yoshino they met three earthly deities, Niemotsu-no-ko (贄持之子), Ihika (井氷鹿) and Iwaoshiwaku-no-ko (石押分之子), who are regarded as the ancestors, respectively, of the cormorant fishers of 阿陀 (reading unconfirmed), the Yoshino no Obito (吉野首), and the 国巣 (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino.

After leaving Hyūga, the party was entertained at 宇沙 (reading unconfirmed), then stayed one year at the 岡田宮, seven years at the 多祁理宮 and eight years at the 高嶋宮 (readings unconfirmed). At 速吸門 (reading unconfirmed) they took on as guide an earthly deity who knew the sea routes, and named him Saonetsuhiko (槁根津日子).

In the Nihon Shoki, the person met at 速吸之門 (reading unconfirmed) is 珍彦 (reading unconfirmed; later 椎根津彦), and the meeting happens just after departure, before Usa (宇佐). The stay at the 高嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi is also given as three years, which differs from the order and the numbers of years in the Kojiki.

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names notes that the Kojiki writes Itsuse-no-Mikoto's death with “崩,” the character it uses for the death of an emperor, whereas the Nihon Shoki writes “薨,” used for the death of princes and the like, and it introduces the view that there was originally a tradition in which Itsuse-no-Mikoto was the hero of the eastern expedition.

story.text: 神倭伊波禮毘古命 (reading unconfirmed) and his elder brother Itsuse-no-Mikoto, the two of them, were at the Takachiho palace and discussed where they should live in order to govern the realm peacefully, and they decided to go east. Setting out from Hyūga, they went toward Tsukushi, and at 宇沙 (reading unconfirmed) in 豊国 (reading unconfirmed) the local people 宇沙都比古 and 宇沙都比賣 (readings unconfirmed) built the “足一騰宮” and presented a feast. After that they stayed one year at the 岡田宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi, seven years at the 多祁理宮 (reading unconfirmed) in the land of 阿岐 (reading unconfirmed), and eight years at the 高嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi.

As they went up from Kibi, at 速吸門 (reading unconfirmed) they met a man who came riding on the shell of a turtle, fishing, and flapping his arms like wings. He was an earthly deity named 宇豆毘古 (reading unconfirmed); he knew the sea routes well and answered that he would serve them. So they held out a pole to him, drew him into the imperial boat, and gave him the name Saonetsuhiko (槁根津日子). A note in the original text makes him the ancestor of the provincial chiefs of Yamato (倭国造) and others.

When they passed the crossing of Naniwa (浪速) and moored their boats at 白肩津 (reading unconfirmed) of 青雲 (reading unconfirmed), 登美能那賀須泥毘古 (reading unconfirmed) raised an army and lay in wait for them. Because they took the shields that had been placed in the boats and went ashore, that place is called 楯津 (reading unconfirmed; now 日下之蓼津). In this battle Itsuse-no-Mikoto was struck in the hand by an arrow of 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed), and he said, “Though I am the child of the sun deity, it was wrong of me to fight facing the sun. From now on let us circle round and strike with the sun on our backs,” and they went round to the south. He washed the blood from his hand in the sea of 血沼 (reading unconfirmed), and at the 男之水門 (reading unconfirmed) in the land of Kii (紀国) he cried out valiantly, “Am I to die of a wound from a base fellow's hand?” and died (the original writes “崩”). His tomb is at 竈山 (reading unconfirmed) in Kii.

When they reached the village of Kumano, a great bear dimly appeared and at once vanished. Then 神倭伊波禮毘古命 (reading unconfirmed) suddenly became “遠延” (a word written phonetically), and all his troops fell prostrate. Just then 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed) of Kumano came bringing a sword and presented it, and the Child of the Heavenly Deities rose, saying, “I have slept long.” When he received the sword, the violent deities of the mountains of Kumano were cut down of themselves, and the troops who had fallen all awoke.

高倉下 (reading unconfirmed) explained how he had come by the sword. In a dream, Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照大神) and 高木神 (reading unconfirmed) summoned Takemikazuchi-no-Kami and commanded him to go down, since the Central Land of the Reed Plains seemed to be in uproar and their children were not at peace. Takemikazuchi-no-Kami answered that even if he did not go down himself, there was the sword with which he had once pacified that land, and it would be enough to send that down. He told 高倉下 that he would make a hole in the roof of his storehouse and drop the sword in, and that he should find it in the morning and present it to the Child of the Heavenly Deities. When he awoke and looked in the storehouse, the sword was truly there, so he presented it. According to a note in the original text, this sword is also called 佐士布都神 (reading unconfirmed), 甕布都神 (reading unconfirmed) and Futsunomitama (布都御魂), and it is at Isonokami Shrine (石上神宮).

Further, 高木大神 (reading unconfirmed) instructed that they must not go on into the interior from there, since there were many violent deities, and that he would send Yatagarasu (八咫烏) from heaven, so they should follow behind it. As they advanced following Yatagarasu, at the lower reaches of the Yoshino River they met Niemotsu-no-ko (贄持之子; ancestor of the cormorant fishers of 阿陀 (reading unconfirmed)), who was catching fish with a fish trap. Next they met Ihika (井氷鹿; ancestor of the Yoshino no Obito and others), a man with a tail who came out of a shining well, and when they entered the mountains, Iwaoshiwaku-no-ko (石押分之子; ancestor of the 国巣 (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino), a man with a tail who came out pushing the rocks apart, came to meet them. All three gave their names as earthly deities. From there they crossed over the mountain paths and entered Uda (宇陀), and so that place is called “the 穿 of Uda” (宇陀之穿; reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The brothers' discussion: where should we live in order to govern the realm peacefully? Let us go east after all.
The words of Itsuse-no-Mikoto: since I am the child of the sun deity, it was wrong to fight facing the sun.
He cried out valiantly, “Am I to die of a wound received from a base fellow?” and died. It is said that the name 男水門 (reading unconfirmed) comes from this.
The oracle of 高木大神 (reading unconfirmed): I will now send Yatagarasu from heaven, and that crow will guide you on the way.

figures.name: Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀬命)
figures.role: Elder brother of 神倭伊波禮毘古命 (reading unconfirmed; the original reads “伊呂兄”). He goes east together with him and, from an arrow wound received from 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed), dies at the 男之水門 (reading unconfirmed) in the land of Kii.

figures.name: 宇沙都比古 and 宇沙都比賣 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Local people of 宇沙 (reading unconfirmed) in 豊国 (reading unconfirmed). They built the 足一騰宮 (reading unconfirmed) and presented a feast to the party.

figures.name: Saonetsuhiko (槁根津日子; originally named 宇豆毘古)
figures.role: An earthly deity who appeared at 速吸門 (reading unconfirmed) riding on a turtle's shell. Because he knew the sea routes, he was drawn into the boat and given this name. He is regarded as the ancestor of the provincial chiefs of Yamato (倭国造) and others.

figures.name: 登美能那賀須泥毘古 (reading unconfirmed; also 登美毘古)
figures.role: Raised an army at 白肩津 (reading unconfirmed) to attack the party, and wounded Itsuse-no-Mikoto with his arrow.

figures.name: Kumano-no-yama-no-araburu-kami (熊野山之荒神)
figures.role: The violent deities of the mountains of Kumano. When the sword was presented, they were cut down of themselves.

figures.name: 熊野之高倉下 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A person of Kumano (a note in the original says “此者人名,” this is a person's name). Following the instructions of a dream, he presented the sword that had been dropped into his storehouse to the Child of the Heavenly Deities, who had fallen prostrate.

figures.name: Yatagarasu (八咫烏)
figures.role: The crow sent from heaven by 高木大神 (reading unconfirmed). It guided the way beyond Kumano.

figures.name: Niemotsu-no-ko (贄持之子)
figures.role: An earthly deity who was catching fish with a fish trap at the lower reaches of the Yoshino River. He is regarded as the ancestor of the cormorant fishers of 阿陀 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Ihika (井氷鹿)
figures.role: An earthly deity with a tail who came out of a shining well. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Yoshino no Obito and others.

figures.name: Iwaoshiwaku-no-ko (石押分之子)
figures.role: An earthly deity with a tail who came out pushing the rocks apart. Hearing that the Child of the Heavenly Deities was coming, he came out to meet him. He is regarded as the ancestor of the 国巣 (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 甲寅, winter, 10th month (丁巳朔辛酉)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the meeting with a fisherman at 速吸之門 (reading unconfirmed) takes place right after setting out on the eastern expedition, before reaching Usa (宇佐). The fisherman's name is 珍彦 (reading unconfirmed), and he is granted the name 椎根津彦 (reading unconfirmed) (in the Kojiki, the meeting comes after leaving Kibi, and 宇豆毘古 is named Saonetsuhiko).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, 5th month (丙寅朔癸酉)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Itsuse-no-Mikoto strokes his sword and gives a war cry at the 山城水門 (reading unconfirmed) of 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed) (the place is called 雄水門 (reading unconfirmed)), then dies at 竈山 (reading unconfirmed) in the land of Kii and is buried at 竈山. His death is written “薨” (in the Kojiki, he cries out at the 男之水門 and “崩,” and his tomb is at 竈山).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, 6th month (乙未朔丁巳)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, those who appear in 高倉下's dream are Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照太神) and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami (武甕雷神), and 高木神 (reading unconfirmed) does not appear. Also, the sending of Yatagarasu (頭八咫烏) is announced by Amaterasu-Ōmikami in the emperor's own dream (in the Kojiki, 高木大神 announces it).

jinmu-uda.title: Uda, 忍坂, 登美毘古 and the Kume Songs (readings unconfirmed)
jinmu-uda.lead: In Uda, 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) is caught in the trap he himself set in a hall and dies, and at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed) the Eighty Braves (八十建) of the earth-spiders (土雲) are struck down all at once at the signal of a song. In the following scenes of attacking 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed) and 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed), songs containing words such as “久米能古良” are set down one after another.

points.text: 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) of Uda pretended to submit and set a crushing trap (押機) in a hall, but it was exposed through the secret report of 弟宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed); driven in by 道臣命 and 大久米命 (readings unconfirmed), he died in his own trap. That place is called the Blood Field of Uda (宇陀之血原).

In the great pit-dwelling (大室) at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed), each of the Eighty Braves (八十建) was entertained with a cook-servant (膳夫) bearing a sword assigned to him, and, as signalled by the order “When you hear the song, cut them down all at once,” they were struck down at one stroke in time with the song.

道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) is recorded as the ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji and others, and 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) as the ancestor of the Kume no Atai and others. The songs in this section contain the words “久米能古” and “久米能古良”.

The part about the fighting with 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed) and with 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed) consists almost entirely of songs, and the course of the fighting and its outcome are not written. In the next section (C16), it is summed up that Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (邇藝速日命) came to present himself, and that the violent deities and the people who would not submit were subdued.

The Kojiki gives no name to these songs, but the Nihon Shoki calls the songs of the same scenes “來目歌” (Kume songs). In the Nihon Shoki, it is 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) alone who questions 兄猾 (reading unconfirmed), and in the fighting with Nagasunebiko (長髄彦) a golden kite alights on the emperor's bow.

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names introduces a view that takes “宇加比賀登母” (the band of cormorant fishers) in the song of the scene with 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed) to refer to the cormorant fishers of 阿陀 (reading unconfirmed), whose ancestor was Niemotsu-no-ko (贄持之子), met in Yoshino, and which points to a connection between the cormorant fishers of 阿陀 and the Kume-be (来目部).

story.text: In Uda there were two brothers, 兄宇迦斯 and 弟宇迦斯 (readings unconfirmed). First, Yatagarasu (八咫烏) was sent to ask whether they would serve, since the Child of the Heavenly Deities had come, but 兄宇迦斯 shot the messenger back with a whistling arrow (鳴鏑). The place where that whistling arrow fell is called 訶夫羅前 (reading unconfirmed). 兄宇迦斯 meant to meet them in battle but could not gather an army, so he pretended to serve, built a large hall, made a crushing trap (押機; a device that crushes) inside it, and lay in wait.

弟宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) came first to present himself and revealed his elder brother's scheme. Then the two, 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji and others, and 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the Kume no Atai and others, summoned 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) and reviled him, telling him to go first himself into the hall he had built and show plainly how he meant to serve. When the two drove him in, gripping the hilts of their swords, pointing their spears and fitting arrows to their bows, 兄宇迦斯 was struck by the crushing trap he himself had made, and died. Because they dragged him out and cut him to pieces, that place is called the Blood Field of Uda (宇陀之血原).

The feast presented by 弟宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) was all distributed among the troops, and a song was sung at this time (C3). After the song there are notes on words in the song, and one of them is recorded as being “a thing of mocking laughter.” 弟宇迦斯 is regarded as the ancestor of the water-bearers (水取) of Uda and others.

When they advanced from there and reached the great pit-dwelling (大室) at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed), the Eighty Braves (八十建) of the tailed earth-spiders (土雲) were waiting in that dwelling. By command of the Child of the Heavenly Deities, the Eighty Braves were given a feast, one cook-servant (膳夫) was assigned to each of them, and each servant was made to carry a sword. They were instructed in advance, “When you hear the song, cut them down all at once,” and when the song was sung (C6), they drew their swords and struck them down at one stroke.

After that, a song was sung when they were about to attack 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed), and two further songs are recorded in succession (C9, C11, C13). Each of these songs has a line resembling “宇知弖斯夜麻牟”. Also, when they attacked 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed), the troops were for a while exhausted, and a song was sung (C15). In this part the Kojiki only sets down the songs in a row, and does not write how the fight with 登美毘古 was settled.

quotes.note: 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) was struck by the crushing trap he himself had made, and died.
The order to the cook-servants: when you hear the song, cut them down all at once.
The opening of the song sung when they were about to attack 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed) (C8). It is written in man'yōgana, one character per syllable.
When they attacked 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed), the troops were for a while exhausted. A song follows after this.

figures.name: 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of Uda. He shot back the messenger Yatagarasu with a whistling arrow and set a crushing trap in a hall, but died in his own trap.

figures.name: 弟宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Revealed his elder brother's scheme, submitted, and presented a feast. He is regarded as the ancestor of the water-bearers (水取) of Uda and others.

figures.name: 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji and others. Together with 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) he drove 兄宇迦斯 into the hall.

figures.name: 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the Kume no Atai and others. Together with 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) he drove 兄宇迦斯 into the hall.

figures.name: Yatagarasu (八咫烏)
figures.role: Sent as messenger to 兄宇迦斯 and 弟宇迦斯 (readings unconfirmed) of Uda, and shot back by 兄宇迦斯 with a whistling arrow.

figures.name: Eighty Braves of the tailed earth-spiders (生尾土雲八十建)
figures.role: The tailed earth-spiders waiting in the great pit-dwelling at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed). At the feast, they were struck down by the cook-servants at the signal of a song.

figures.name: Crushing trap (押機)
figures.role: The device 兄宇迦斯 (reading unconfirmed) made inside the hall. 兄宇迦斯 himself was struck by it and died.

figures.name: 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The foe the expedition sets out to attack. In this scene songs are simply set down in a row, and the outcome of the fight is not written.

figures.name: 兄師木 and 弟師木 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Foes attacked by the party. It is recorded that in this fighting the troops were for a while exhausted.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, autumn, 8th month (甲午朔乙未)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the one sent to verify the scheme of 兄猾 (reading unconfirmed; 兄宇迦斯) is 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) alone, and the name of 大久米命 does not appear. The song at the banquet after 兄猾 dies by stepping on his own device is called a “來目歌” (Kume song).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, winter, 10th month (癸巳朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, it is stated explicitly that the one who sings the signal song at the banquet in the great pit-dwelling at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed) is 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) (the Kojiki does not say who sings).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, 12th month (癸巳朔丙申)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, in the fighting with Nagasunebiko (長髄彦; 登美毘古), a golden kite flies in and alights on the tip of the emperor's bow, and its light leaves the enemy soldiers unable to fight. This story of the kite is not in the Kojiki.

jinmu-sokui.title: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto Comes to Serve, and the Choice of an Empress
jinmu-sokui.lead: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (邇藝速日命), who had come down from heaven, presents himself before the Child of the Heavenly Deities and serves him, and the Child of the Heavenly Deities rules the realm from the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮) at Unebi (畝火). As empress, 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Ōmononushi-no-Kami of Miwa (美和), is welcomed, through the mediation of 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) and an exchange of songs.

points.text: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto came down from heaven following the Child of the Heavenly Deities, presented heavenly tokens (天津瑞) and served him. Umashimaji-no-Mikoto (宇摩志麻遲命), born to him and the younger sister of 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed), is regarded as the ancestor of the Mononobe no Muraji (物部連), the 穂積臣 (reading unconfirmed) and the 婇臣 (reading unconfirmed).
After subduing the violent deities and the people who would not submit, the Child of the Heavenly Deities ruled the realm from the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮) at Unebi (畝火).

伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), who became empress, was a daughter born after Ōmononushi-no-Kami of Miwa (美和) turned himself into a vermilion-painted arrow and visited 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed), and for that reason she was called “the child of a deity.” Her original name was 富登多多良伊須須岐比賣命 (reading unconfirmed).

With 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) acting as go-between, 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) was chosen from among seven maidens at 高佐士野 (reading unconfirmed). Songs are exchanged between the emperor and 大久米命, and between the maiden and 大久米命.

In the Nihon Shoki, the empress Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (媛蹈韛五十鈴媛命) is said to be the child of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed; daughter of 三嶋溝橛耳神 (reading unconfirmed)), so her parents differ from those in the Kojiki, Ōmononushi-no-Kami and 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed; daughter of 三嶋湟咋 (reading unconfirmed)). Also, in the Nihon Shoki, Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (饒速日命) kills Nagasunebiko (長髄彦) and submits, and the accession is placed in spring, 1st month, of the year 辛酉.

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names states that, whereas the Kojiki's account of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto is brief, the Nihon Shoki's account has a stronger character as a tradition telling of the deeds of the founding ancestor of the Mononobe clan, and it notes that views are divided on which is the older form.

story.text: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto came to present himself and said that, having heard that the Child of the Heavenly Deities had come down from heaven, he had come down following after him; he presented heavenly tokens (天津瑞) and served him. Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto took as his wife 登美夜毘賣 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed), and Umashimaji-no-Mikoto (宇摩志麻遲命) was born. A note in the original text makes him the ancestor of the Mononobe no Muraji, the 穂積臣 (reading unconfirmed) and the 婇臣 (reading unconfirmed). Thus, having made the violent deities submit and driven off the people who would not submit, he ruled the realm from the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮) at Unebi (畝火).

When the emperor was in Hyūga, he had taken as his wife 阿比良比賣 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of the 小椅君 of 阿多 (readings unconfirmed), and had two children, 多藝志美美命 (reading unconfirmed) and 岐須美美命 (reading unconfirmed). But when he looked anew for a woman to make his chief consort, 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) said, “Here there is a maiden who is called the child of a deity.”

The reason that maiden was called the child of a deity is as follows. 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 三嶋湟咋 (reading unconfirmed), was beautiful, and Ōmononushi-no-Kami of Miwa (美和) saw her and was drawn to her. Ōmononushi-no-Kami changed himself into a vermilion-painted arrow, floated down the ditch where the maiden was relieving herself, and struck her 富登 (private parts). The startled maiden took the arrow home and laid it beside her bed, and at once the arrow became a fine man, who took her as his wife. The child born was 富登多多良伊須須岐比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), who later, disliking the word “富登,” changed her name to 比賣多多良伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed).

Seven maidens were amusing themselves at 高佐士野 (reading unconfirmed), and 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) was among them. 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) saw them and addressed the emperor in a song (C17). The emperor knew in his heart that 伊須氣余理比賣 was standing at the very front, and answered in a song (C19).

When 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed) conveyed the emperor's words to 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), she saw 大久米命's sharp, tattooed eyes, found them strange, and asked about them in a song (C21). 大久米命 also answered in a song (C23), and the maiden said that she would serve. The maiden's house was beside the Sai River (狭井河), and the emperor went there and spent a night with her. A note in the original text records that because there were many 山由理草 (lily plants) by the river, and their original name was “佐韋,” it was named the Sai River (佐韋河). Later, when the maiden came to the palace, the emperor composed a song (C25).

quotes.note: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto presented heavenly tokens and served him.
Dwelling at the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮) at Unebi, he ruled the realm.
Ōmononushi-no-Kami changed himself into a vermilion-painted arrow and floated down the ditch.
Then the maiden (伊須氣余理比賣, reading unconfirmed) said that she would serve.

figures.name: 登美夜毘賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed). She became the wife of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto and bore Umashimaji-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: 阿比良比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of the 小椅君 of 阿多 (readings unconfirmed). The emperor's wife while he was in Hyūga; she bore 多藝志美美命 and 岐須美美命 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 多藝志美美命 and 岐須美美命 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Children of the emperor and 阿比良比賣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大久米命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Recommended 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) as chief consort and mediated between the emperor and the maiden through songs. The maiden wondered at his tattooed eyes.

figures.name: 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 三嶋湟咋 (reading unconfirmed). She was united with Ōmononushi-no-Kami, who had turned into a vermilion-painted arrow, and bore 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 三嶋湟咋 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Vermilion-painted arrow (丹塗矢)
figures.role: The form Ōmononushi-no-Kami changed himself into. When it was laid beside the bed, it became a fine man.

figures.name: Heavenly tokens (天津瑞)
figures.role: The tokens Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto presented to the Child of the Heavenly Deities.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 戊午, 12th month (癸巳朔丙申)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (饒速日命) is the lord whom Nagasunebiko (長髄彦) serves; after the emperor and Nagasunebiko show each other tokens of being children of the heavenly deities (a heavenly feathered arrow, 天羽羽矢, and a quiver, 歩靫), Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto kills Nagasunebiko and submits, leading his troops. In the Kojiki, Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto merely comes to present himself and offers heavenly tokens (天津瑞), and there is no story of killing 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, record before accession, the year 庚申, autumn, 8th month (癸丑朔戊辰)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (媛蹈韛五十鈴媛命), welcomed as principal consort, is said to be the child of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 三嶋溝橛耳神 (reading unconfirmed). In the Kojiki, her father is Ōmononushi-no-Kami of Miwa (美和), and her mother is 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 三嶋湟咋 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, 1st year, the year 辛酉, spring, 1st month (庚辰朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, he accedes at the Kashihara palace (橿原宮) in spring, 1st month, of the year 辛酉 (庚辰朔), and this year is made the emperor's first year. The Kojiki records that he ruled the realm from the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮), but gives no year or month.

tagishimimi.title: The Rebellion of Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto
tagishimimi.lead: After Emperor Jinmu died, Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto (當藝志美美命), an elder half-brother, took the empress 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) as his wife and plotted to kill his three younger half-brothers. Of the younger brothers, who learned of this through their mother's songs, the youngest, 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed), struck down Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto, and, with the throne yielded to him by his elder brother Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto, ruled the realm.

points.text: When Emperor Jinmu died, Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto, the elder half-brother born in Hyūga, took the empress 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) as his wife and plotted to kill her children, his three younger half-brothers. 伊須氣余理比賣 warned the princes of the danger in songs.

The elder brother Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto trembled hand and foot and could not kill Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto, so the younger brother 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed) took the weapon from his elder brother and struck him down. Because of this deed, 神沼河耳命 was also called 建沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed).

Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto, saying that since he had failed to kill the enemy he should not stand above, even though he was the elder, yielded the position to his younger brother and became a ritual abstainer (忌人) to serve him. Thus 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suizei) ruled the realm.
Emperor Jinmu's age is recorded as one hundred and thirty-seven years, and his tomb as being on top of 白檮尾 (reading unconfirmed), north of Mount Unebi (畝火山).

In the Nihon Shoki, a bow and arrow are used to strike down 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed; Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto), and those targeted are “two younger brothers” (二弟). Emperor Jinmu's age is also given as one hundred and twenty-seven years, which differs from the Kojiki.

story.text: The children born to 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) were three: 日子八井命 (reading unconfirmed), Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto (神八井耳命) and 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed). After the emperor died, their elder half-brother Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto took 伊須氣余理比賣, who had been the emperor's principal wife, as his wife and plotted to kill his three younger brothers. Their mother 伊須氣余理比賣, distressed by this, warned the princes in songs (C27, C29). The words “佐韋賀波” (the Sai River, 狭井河) and “宇泥備夜麻” (Mount Unebi, 畝傍山) appear in the songs.

The princes were startled to hear this and resolved to kill Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto. 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed) asked his elder brother Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto to take a weapon, go in and kill Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto. Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto went in with the weapon, but his hands and feet trembled (written phonetically in the original as “和那那岐弖”) and he could not kill him. So the younger brother 神沼河耳命 asked for the weapon his elder brother was holding, went in and killed Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto. For this reason 神沼河耳命 is also called 建沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed).

Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto yielded the position to his younger brother, saying: “I could not kill the enemy, but you were able to kill him. Therefore, though I am the elder, I should not stand above. You shall stand above and rule the realm. I will help you and serve you as a ritual abstainer (忌人).” A note in the original text makes 日子八井命 (reading unconfirmed) the ancestor of the 茨田連 and 手嶋連 (readings unconfirmed), and Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto the ancestor of many lineages, including the 意富臣, the 小子部連, the 阿蘇君 and the provincial chiefs of Shinano (科野国造) (readings unconfirmed). 神沼河耳命 ruled the realm.
It is recorded that the age of this emperor 神倭伊波禮毘古 (reading unconfirmed) was one hundred and thirty-seven years, and that his tomb is on top of 白檮尾 (reading unconfirmed), north of Mount Unebi (畝火山).

quotes.note: When Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto was plotting to kill his three younger brothers.
Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto trembled hand and foot and could not kill him.
The words of Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto: I could not kill the enemy, but you have already killed the enemy.
Emperor Jinmu's age was one hundred and thirty-seven years.

figures.name: Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto (當藝志美美命)
figures.role: Son of 阿比良比賣 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor's wife while he was in Hyūga. After the emperor's death he took 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed) as his wife and tried to kill his three younger half-brothers, and was struck down by 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 日子八井命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Eldest son of 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed). Regarded as the ancestor of the 茨田連 and 手嶋連 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed; also 建沼河耳命, Emperor Suizei)
figures.role: Youngest son of 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed). He took the weapon from his elder brother and struck down Tagishimimi-no-Mikoto, and ruled the realm after his elder brother yielded to him.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 4, Emperor Suizei, record before accession, the year 己卯, winter, 11th month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 神渟名川耳尊 (reading unconfirmed; 神沼河耳命) has a bow and arrows made and targets 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed); at 片丘 (reading unconfirmed), where 手研耳命 was sleeping alone on a large bed, he takes the bow and arrows from his elder brother, who is trembling and cannot shoot, and shoots him dead. The Kojiki writes only “兵” (weapon) and does not record the place either.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 4, Emperor Suizei, record before accession
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, those targeted by 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed) are “two younger brothers” (二弟), and in the record of Emperor Jinmu as well, the princes born to the empress are two, 神八井命 (reading unconfirmed) and 神渟名川耳尊 (reading unconfirmed). In the Kojiki they are three younger brothers (日子八井命, Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto and 神沼河耳命).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 3, Emperor Jinmu, 76th year, spring, 3rd month (甲午朔甲辰)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Jinmu dies at the Kashihara palace (橿原宮) in spring, 3rd month, of his 76th year (甲午朔甲辰), at the age of one hundred and twenty-seven, and is buried the following year in a tomb north-east of Mount Unebi (畝傍山). In the Kojiki he is one hundred and thirty-seven, and his tomb is on top of 白檮尾 (reading unconfirmed), north of Mount Unebi (畝火山).

kesshi.title: From Emperor Suizei to Emperor Kaika
kesshi.lead: For the eight reigns from Emperor Suizei to Emperor Kaika, the Kojiki records chiefly the names of the palaces, the wives and children, which lineages each was the ancestor of, and the ages and tombs. Among these are accounts that connect to later stories, such as the pacification of Kibi, the birth of Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰), and the genealogy running from the descendants of 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) to 息長帶比賣命 (reading unconfirmed).

points.text: The accounts of these eight reigns center on genealogy, recording palaces, wives and children, the ancestors of lineages, ages and tombs, and there is hardly any narrative. Among them, the section on Emperor Kōrei records that 大吉備津日子命 (Ōkibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto) and 若建吉備津日子命 (reading unconfirmed) pacified the land of Kibi, using Harima (針間) as the entrance.

The section on Emperor Kōgen records that Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰) was born as the son of 比古布都押之信命 (reading unconfirmed), and that his nine children became the ancestors of many lineages, such as the 波多臣, the 許勢臣, the Soga no Omi (蘇我臣), the 平群臣 and the 木臣 (readings unconfirmed).

The section on Emperor Kaika records a long genealogy of the descendants of 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed), from 沙本毘古王 (Sahobiko; 王 reading unconfirmed) and 沙本毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed) down to the later 息長帶比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), and people who appear in later stories of Part 2 are introduced here.

In the Nihon Shoki, 彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed; 比古布都押之信命) is said to be Takeuchi-no-Sukune's “grandfather,” a generation removed from the Kojiki's “father.” Also, Emperor Suizei's age is given as eighty-four, which differs from the Kojiki's forty-five.

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names introduces a view that takes the marriage of 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) to the daughter of Ame-no-Mikage-no-Kami (天之御影神), the deity of Mount 三上 (reading unconfirmed) in Ōmi (近江), as showing a connection with the Ōmi region.

story.text: 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suizei) ruled the realm from the 高岡宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Katsuragi (葛城), and took as his wife 河俣毘賣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 師木県主 (reading unconfirmed), and 師木津日子玉手見命 (reading unconfirmed) was born. His age was forty-five, and his tomb is at 衝田岡 (reading unconfirmed). 師木津日子玉手見命 (Emperor Annei) ruled from the 浮穴宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 片鹽 (reading unconfirmed); he had three children with 阿久斗比賣 (reading unconfirmed), and 大倭日子鉏友命 (reading unconfirmed) succeeded him. His age was forty-nine, and his tomb is at 美富登 (reading unconfirmed) on Mount Unebi (畝火山).

大倭日子鉏友命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Itoku) ruled from the 境岡宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 輕 (reading unconfirmed); his age was forty-five, and his tomb is above 眞名子谷 (reading unconfirmed) on Mount Unebi. 御眞津日子訶惠志泥命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kōshō) ruled from the 掖上宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Katsuragi, and his elder brother 天押帶日子命 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as the ancestor of many lineages, such as the 春日臣, the 小野臣 and the 柿本臣 (readings unconfirmed). His age was ninety-three, and his tomb is on top of 博多山 (reading unconfirmed) at 掖上. 大倭帶日子國押人命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kōan) ruled from the 秋津嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 室 (reading unconfirmed) in Katsuragi and took as his wife his niece 忍鹿比賣命 (reading unconfirmed); his age was one hundred and twenty-three, and his tomb is on top of 玉手岡 (reading unconfirmed).

大倭根子日子賦斗邇命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kōrei) ruled from the 廬戸宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 黒田 (reading unconfirmed), and had eight children. Among them were 夜麻登登母母曾毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed), 大吉備津日子命 (Ōkibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto; also called 比古伊佐勢理毘古命, reading unconfirmed) and Wakahiko-Takekibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto (若日子建吉備津日子命). The two, 大吉備津日子命 and 若建吉備津日子命 (reading unconfirmed), set sacred jars (忌瓮) at the 氷河 (reading unconfirmed) cape in Harima (針間), and, using Harima as the entrance, subdued the land of Kibi by words and pacified it. His age was one hundred and six, and his tomb is on top of 馬坂 (reading unconfirmed) at 片岡 (reading unconfirmed).

大倭根子日子國玖琉命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kōgen) ruled from the 堺原宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 輕 (reading unconfirmed); his children included Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大毘古命), 若倭根子日子大毘毘命 (reading unconfirmed), 比古布都押之信命 (reading unconfirmed) and 建波邇夜須毘古命 (reading unconfirmed). Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto (建沼河別命), son of Ōbiko-no-Mikoto, is regarded as the ancestor of the Abe no Omi (阿倍臣) and others. 比古布都押之信命 took as his wife 山下影日賣 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 宇豆比古 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the provincial chiefs of 木国 (木国造; reading unconfirmed), and the child born was Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰). The nine children of Takeuchi-no-Sukune are regarded as the ancestors of the 波多臣, the 許勢臣, the Soga no Omi (蘇我臣), the 平群臣, the 木臣 and the 玉手臣 of Katsuragi (readings unconfirmed), among others. His age was fifty-seven, and his tomb is on top of 中岡 (reading unconfirmed) at 劔池 (reading unconfirmed).

若倭根子日子大毘毘命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kaika) ruled from the 伊邪河宮 (reading unconfirmed) at Kasuga (春日), and took as his wife his father's consort (庶母) 伊迦賀色許賣命 (reading unconfirmed), and 御眞木入日子印惠命 (reading unconfirmed) was born; this child succeeded him. 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed), his child by another wife, 意祁都比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), had eleven children, among them 沙本毘古王 (Sahobiko; 王 reading unconfirmed) and 沙本毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed), who became the empress of 伊久米天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suinin). 日子坐王 also took as his wife 息長水依比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Ame-no-Mikage-no-Kami, who is worshipped by the priest (祝) of 御上 (reading unconfirmed) in 近淡海 (Ōmi). Further, from 山代之大筒木眞若王 (reading unconfirmed), whom 日子坐王 fathered by taking as his wife his mother's younger sister 袁祁都比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), the genealogy continues through 迦邇米雷王 and 息長宿禰王 (readings unconfirmed), and 息長帶比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) is born as a child of 息長宿禰王. His age was sixty-three, and his tomb is on top of the slope of 伊邪河 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suizei) dwelt at the 高岡宮 (reading unconfirmed) in Katsuragi and ruled the realm. Each of the following reigns begins with the same opening formula.
Using Harima as the entrance, they subdued the land of Kibi by words and pacified it.
比古布都押之信命 (reading unconfirmed) took 山下影日賣 (reading unconfirmed) as his wife, and Takeuchi-no-Sukune was born.
As children of 息長宿禰王 (reading unconfirmed), 息長帶比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) and others were born.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 4, Emperor Kōgen, 7th year, spring, 2nd month (丙寅朔丁卯)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed) is said to be the grandfather of Takeuchi-no-Sukune (武内宿禰). In the Kojiki, Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰) is the son of 比古布都押之信命 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 4, Emperor Suizei, 33rd year, summer, 5th month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Suizei falls ill in summer, 5th month, of his 33rd year and dies at the age of eighty-four. In the Kojiki his age is given as forty-five.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 10th year, 9th month (丙戌朔甲午)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, there is no story of the pacification of Kibi in the record of Emperor Kōrei, and it is in the 9th month of the 10th year of Emperor Sujin that 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) is sent to the western circuit (西道). In the Kojiki, in the section on Emperor Kōrei, 大吉備津日子命 (Ōkibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto) and 若建吉備津日子命 (reading unconfirmed) pacify the land of Kibi.

sujin-miwa.title: Emperor Sujin and Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami of Miwa
sujin-miwa.lead: When a pestilence spread in the time of Emperor Sujin, Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami (大物主大神) appeared in a dream and declared that if he were worshipped by 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed), the land would be at peace; when he was worshipped accordingly, the pestilence ceased. As the reason 意富多多泥古 was known to be a descendant of the deity, the story is told that when the man who visited 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed) was traced by a hemp thread, it led to the shrine on Mount Miwa (美和山).

points.text: In the time of Emperor Sujin, when people were on the verge of dying out from pestilence, Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami declared in a dream, “This comes from my will,” and asked to be worshipped by 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed). When the emperor sought out 意富多多泥古 from the village of 美努 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi and had him worship as the officiating priest at Mount 御諸 (reading unconfirmed), the pestilence ceased.

A hemp thread was stuck into the garment of the man who visited 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed) night after night, and when the thread was followed, it led to the shrine of the deity of Mount Miwa (美和山). It is recorded that because three loops (三勾) of hemp were left over, that place is called “Miwa” (美和).

To quell the pestilence, shrines for the heavenly and earthly deities (天神地祇) were established besides Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami; red shields and spears were offered to Sumisaka-no-Kami (墨坂神) of Uda and black shields and spears to Ōsaka-no-Kami (大坂神), and offerings (幣帛) were also made to the deities of the slopes and of the river shallows.

In the Nihon Shoki, Ōmononushi-no-Kami first possesses Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命) and demands worship, and 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed; 意富多多泥古) is found at 陶邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 茅渟県 (reading unconfirmed) and gives his name as the child of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed). In the Kojiki, he is found in the village of 美努 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi and is a descendant in the fourth generation from Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami.

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names introduces a view that the Kojiki's depiction of Ōmononushi-no-Kami going out through the keyhole of the door hints that his form is that of a snake, and states that in the record of the 9th month of the 10th year of Emperor Sujin in the Nihon Shoki it is revealed as a “small snake” (小蛇).

The Kokugakuin University database of deity names introduces a view that the worship of the deities of 墨坂 (Sumisaka; an important route on the east of Yamato) and 大坂 (Ōsaka; an important route on the west of Yamato) was the worship of boundary deities to prevent the pestilence from entering.

story.text: 御眞木入日子印惠命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin) ruled the realm from the 水垣宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 師木 (reading unconfirmed). With three wives he had twelve children (seven sons and five daughters), and 伊久米伊理毘古伊佐知命 (reading unconfirmed) succeeded him. Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto (豊木入日子命) is regarded as the ancestor of the 上毛野君, the 下毛野君 (readings unconfirmed) and others; 豊鉏比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise (伊勢大神); and 大入杵命 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as the ancestor of the 能登臣 (reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that in the time of 倭日子命 (reading unconfirmed) a human fence (人垣) was first set up at a tomb.

In the time of this emperor much pestilence arose, and the people were on the verge of dying out. On a night when the emperor, grieving, was in the sacred bed (神牀), Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami appeared in a dream and declared, “This comes from my will. If you have me worshipped by 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed), the deity's influence will not arise and the land will be at peace.” So swift messengers on horseback were sent out in all directions to search, and that person was found in the village of 美努 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi and brought forward.

When the emperor asked whose child he was, 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed) answered that he was the child of 建甕槌命 (reading unconfirmed), son of 飯肩巣見命 (reading unconfirmed), son of 櫛御方命 (reading unconfirmed), who had been born when Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami took as his wife 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 陶津耳命 (reading unconfirmed). The emperor was greatly pleased and said that the realm would be at peace and the people would prosper. He then made 意富多多泥古 the officiating priest and had him worship 意富美和之大神 (reading unconfirmed) at Mount 御諸 (reading unconfirmed).

Further, he commanded 伊迦賀色許男命 (reading unconfirmed) to make the 天之八十毘羅訶 (reading unconfirmed) and established shrines for the heavenly and earthly deities (天神地祇). He offered red shields and spears to Sumisaka-no-Kami (墨坂神) of Uda and black shields and spears to Ōsaka-no-Kami (大坂神), and made offerings (幣帛), leaving none out, to the deities of the ridges of the slopes and to the deities of the river shallows. By this the pestilence ceased entirely and the land was at peace.

The reason 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed) was known to be the child of a deity is as follows. 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed) was beautiful, and a splendid man beyond compare came visiting her in the night, and soon she conceived. When her parents, finding this strange, asked her about it, she answered that a man whose name she did not know came every night, so her parents told her to scatter red earth in front of the bed and to stick a needle threaded with hemp thread into the hem of the man's garment. When they looked in the morning, the hemp thread had gone out through the keyhole of the door, and only three loops (三勾) of hemp were left in her hands. When they followed the thread, it led to the shrine of the deity of Mount Miwa (美和山), so they knew he was the child of a deity, and because three loops of hemp were left over, that place is called Miwa (美和). A note in the original text makes 意富多多泥古命 the ancestor of the 神君 and the 鴨君 (readings unconfirmed).

quotes.note: Much pestilence arose, and the people were on the verge of dying out.
The oracle of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami: if you have me worshipped by 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed), the deity's influence will not arise and the land will be at peace.
The parents' instruction: thread a needle with hemp thread of “閇蘇” (a word written phonetically) and stick it into the hem of the man's garment.
Because three loops of hemp were left over, that place was named Miwa (美和).

figures.name: 御眞木入日子印惠命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 水垣宮 (reading unconfirmed) at 師木 (reading unconfirmed). Troubled by pestilence, he had Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami worshipped in accordance with the oracle of a dream.

figures.name: 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed; also 意富多多泥古命)
figures.role: A descendant of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami found in the village of 美努 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi. As officiating priest he worshipped 意富美和之大神 (reading unconfirmed) at Mount 御諸 (reading unconfirmed). He is regarded as the ancestor of the 神君 and the 鴨君 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 陶津耳命 (reading unconfirmed). She conceived the child of the divine man who visited her night after night.

figures.name: 陶津耳命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 櫛御方命, 飯肩巣見命 and 建甕槌命 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: The three generations between the child of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 活玉依毘賣 and 意富多多泥古 (建甕槌命 is the father of 意富多多泥古).

figures.name: 伊迦賀色許男命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: At the emperor's command he made the 天之八十毘羅訶 (reading unconfirmed) and established shrines for the heavenly and earthly deities.

figures.name: Sumisaka-no-Kami (墨坂神)
figures.role: A deity of Uda. To quell the pestilence, red shields and spears were offered to him.

figures.name: Ōsaka-no-Kami (大坂神)
figures.role: A deity to whom black shields and spears were offered to quell the pestilence.

figures.name: 豊鉏比賣命 (reading unconfirmed; also 豊鉏入日賣命)
figures.role: Daughter of Emperor Sujin. A note records that she worshipped at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise.

figures.name: 伊久米伊理毘古伊佐知命 (reading unconfirmed; also 伊玖米入日子伊沙知命)
figures.role: Son of Emperor Sujin, who succeeded him and ruled the realm (Emperor Suinin).

figures.name: 倭日子命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Emperor Sujin. It is recorded that in the time of this prince a human fence was first set up at a tomb.

figures.name: Hemp thread (閇蘇紡麻) and three loops (三勾)
figures.role: The hemp thread stuck into the hem of the man's garment to learn who he was. It went through the keyhole and led to the shrine on Mount Miwa, and the three loops left over are regarded as the origin of the place name “Miwa” (美和).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 7th year, spring, 2nd month (丁丑朔辛卯)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, when divination is performed at 神浅茅原 (reading unconfirmed) in the 2nd month of the 7th year of Emperor Sujin, Ōmononushi-no-Kami (大物主神) first possesses Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命) and demands to be worshipped, and afterwards appears in the emperor's dream and tells him to have 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship him. In the Kojiki, only the oracle of the dream is recorded.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 7th year, autumn, 8th month (癸卯朔己酉)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) is found at 陶邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 茅渟県 (reading unconfirmed) and answers that his father is Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and his mother 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed), so he is a child of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami. In the Kojiki, he is found in the village of 美努 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi and is a descendant in the fourth generation from Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, record of the 10th year, 9th month (是後, “after this”)
compare.text: The Nihon Shoki has no story of tracing his identity with a hemp thread; instead it has the story of Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto becoming the wife of Ōmononushi-no-Kami and being startled to see a beautiful small snake in her comb box (the origin of 箸墓 (reading unconfirmed)).

sujin-shido.title: The Dispatch along the Four Circuits and the Rebellion of 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed)
sujin-shido.lead: In the time of Emperor Sujin (御眞木入日子印惠命, reading unconfirmed), Ōbiko-no-Mikoto, Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto and 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) were sent to various regions, and a mysterious song sung by a maiden on the way revealed the treason of 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor's “elder half-brother” (庶兄). It is told that the rebellion was quelled by the arrow of 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed), that Ōbiko-no-Mikoto and his son Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto met at Aizu (相津), and that the realm was brought to order.

points.text: The emperor interpreted the maiden's song that Ōbiko-no-Mikoto had heard at 幣羅坂 (reading unconfirmed) as “a sign that my elder half-brother 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) has formed an evil intent,” and sent Ōbiko-no-Mikoto and 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed) to Yamashiro (山代) to subdue him.

In the battle across the 和訶羅河 (reading unconfirmed), the arrow that 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) shot first missed, while the arrow of 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed) shot 建波邇安王 dead, and the rebel army collapsed completely.

Ōbiko-no-Mikoto, sent along the Koshi road (高志道), and his son Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto, sent along the twelve circuits of the east (東方十二道), met at “Aizu” (相津), and this is given as the origin of that place name. 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to the land of Tanba (旦波國).
After the pacification, the tribute of the bow-tip (弓端之調) from men and the tribute of the fingertips (手末之調) from women were paid for the first time, and the emperor was praised as “所知初國之御眞木天皇”.

In the Nihon Shoki (Emperor Sujin, 10th year, 9th month), four men, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命), Takenunakawawake (武渟川別), 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed), are sent as generals, and the one who interprets the meaning of the maiden's song is not the emperor but Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命).

story.text: In the reign of Emperor Sujin, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto was sent along the Koshi road (高志道) and his son Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto along the twelve circuits of the east (東方十二道), and they were commanded to soften and pacify the people who would not submit (in the original, “麻都漏波奴人等”). Also 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to the land of Tanba (旦波國) and commanded to kill a man called 玖賀耳之御笠 (reading unconfirmed). As Ōbiko-no-Mikoto was heading for the land of Koshi (高志國), a maiden wearing a waist skirt (腰裳) stood at 幣羅坂 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro (山代) and sang a song.

In that song the address “美麻紀伊理毘古波夜” was repeated again and again. Ōbiko-no-Mikoto, finding it strange, turned his horse back and asked what it meant, but the maiden answered, “I said nothing. I only sang a song,” and suddenly vanished, no one knew where. When Ōbiko-no-Mikoto returned to the capital and reported to the emperor, the emperor answered that this was a sign that his elder half-brother 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed), who was in the land of Yamashiro (山代國), had formed an evil intent.

The emperor commanded Ōbiko-no-Mikoto to raise an army and go against him, and sent with him 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 丸邇臣 (reading unconfirmed). The party set sacred jars (忌瓮) at 丸邇坂 (reading unconfirmed) before advancing, and when they reached the 和訶羅河 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro, 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) had raised an army and was waiting for them. Because the two armies faced each other across the river and challenged each other, that place is called 伊杼美 (reading unconfirmed; now 伊豆美). When 日子國夫玖命 asked the other side to shoot their sacred arrow (忌矢) first, the arrow of 建波邇安王 did not hit, while the arrow shot by 國夫玖命 struck 建波邇安王 and killed him.

The army of 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) was utterly defeated and fled in all directions. Because the soldiers, driven into a corner at the crossing of 久須婆 (reading unconfirmed), soiled their loincloths with excrement, that place is called 屎褌 (reading unconfirmed; now 久須婆); because, when the fleeing army was cut off and cut down, they floated on the river like cormorants, that river is called the Cormorant River (鵜河); and because they cut the soldiers down and “波布理” them, that place is called 波布理曾能 (reading unconfirmed).

When the pacification was over and they had reported it, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto set out for the land of Koshi as earlier commanded. Then Takenunakawawake (建沼河別), who had been sent to the east, and his father Ōbiko (大毘古) met at Aizu (相津), and so that place is called Aizu. Thus each pacified the land to which he had been sent and reported, and the realm was at great peace and the people grew rich and prospered. At this time the tribute of the bow-tip (弓端之調) from men and the tribute of the fingertips (手末之調) from women were first levied, and so, in praise of this reign, the emperor is called “所知初國之御眞木天皇”. In this reign the 依網池 (reading unconfirmed) and the 酒折池 (reading unconfirmed) at 輕 (reading unconfirmed) were also made; the emperor died at the age of one hundred and sixty-eight, and his tomb is on top of the hill 勾之岡 (reading unconfirmed) on the 山邊道 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The maiden's answer: “I said nothing. I only sang a song.”
The emperor's words: “This is a sign that my elder half-brother in the land of Yamashiro, 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed), has formed an evil intent.”
It is said that, because of such things as first having tribute paid, this emperor was praised as “所知初國之御眞木天皇”.

figures.name: 御眞木入日子印惠命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin)
figures.role: The emperor of this story. He interpreted the maiden's song as a sign of treason and ordered the rebel to be subdued.

figures.name: 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent to the land of Tanba (旦波國) and commanded to strike down 玖賀耳之御笠 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Maiden wearing a waist skirt (服腰裳少女)
figures.role: The maiden who let Ōbiko-no-Mikoto hear a song at 幣羅坂 (reading unconfirmed), and, when questioned, answered “I only sang” and vanished.

figures.name: 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince of the land of Yamashiro whom the emperor calls his “elder half-brother” (庶兄). He raised an army and lay in wait, but was shot dead by 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 丸邇臣 (reading unconfirmed). Sent with Ōbiko-no-Mikoto, he brought down 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) with an arrow.

figures.name: Sacred jars (忌瓮)
figures.role: The vessels set at 丸邇坂 (reading unconfirmed) when the army set out.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 10th year, 9th month (丙戌朔甲午)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命) is sent to the northern lands (北陸), Takenunakawawake (武渟川別) to the eastern sea region (東海), 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) to the western circuit (西道) and 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed) to Tanba (丹波), and they are given seals and cords of office (印綬) and made generals. In the Kojiki it is 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) who goes to Tanba (旦波), and a dispatch along the western circuit is not written in this section.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 10th year, 9th month (壬子)
compare.text: In the Shoki, the place where the maiden is met is on top of 和珥坂 (reading unconfirmed) (in a “one version says,” 一云, the 平坂 of 山背, readings unconfirmed), and the one who found the song suspicious and declared it a sign of treason is Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命), the emperor's aunt (姑). 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) attacks together with his wife 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed); 吾田媛 is killed at Ōsaka (大坂) by 五十狹芹彦命 (reading unconfirmed), and 武埴安彦, across the 輪韓河 (reading unconfirmed; later called the 挑河), is shot in the chest by 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed) and killed.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 5, Emperor Sujin, 12th year, autumn, 9th month (甲辰朔己丑)
compare.text: In the Shoki, the account of imposing the tribute of the bow-tip (弭調) on men and the tribute of the fingertips (手末調) on women, and of praising the emperor as “御肇國天皇”, is in the 9th month of the 12th year of Emperor Sujin.

sahobiko.title: The Rebellion of 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed)
sahobiko.lead: 沙本毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed), consort of Emperor Suinin (伊久米伊理毘古伊佐知命 (reading unconfirmed)), was handed a small dagger by her elder brother 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed) so that she would stab the emperor to death, but she could not carry it out and confessed everything. When her brother shut himself up in a rice fortress (稻城), the consort went in as well; she handed over to the emperor only the child 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed), who was born amid the flames, and died together with her brother.

points.text: Asked by her elder brother 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed) "Whom do you love more, your husband or your brother?", the consort 沙本毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed) answered "My brother." She was given a cord dagger to kill the emperor, but though she raised it three times she could not stab him, and her falling tears woke the emperor.

Asked by the emperor what his dream meant (a sudden shower coming from 沙本 (reading unconfirmed) and a small brocade-colored snake coiling around his neck), the consort revealed her brother's entire plot, and the emperor raised an army and surrounded the rice fortress (稻城).

The consort entered her brother's rice fortress and sent out only the child born there. Because she had shaved her hair and let her jewel cords and clothes rot beforehand, the emperor's soldiers could not seize her.
Because the child was born amid the fire of the burning rice fortress, he was named 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed). In the end 沙本比古王 (reading unconfirmed) was killed, and the consort died with him.

In the Nihon Shoki, the plot of 狹穗彦王 (reading unconfirmed) is placed in the 9th month of the 4th year of Emperor Suinin, and the emperor's midday nap with his head on the empress's lap, at the 高宮 of 來目 (reading unconfirmed), in the 10th month of the 5th year. The empress carries the prince over the fortress wall and sends him out, recommends the five daughters of 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed) for the inner palace, and then dies inside the fortress together with her brother.

story.text: Emperor Suinin ruled the realm from the 玉垣宮 of 師木 (reading unconfirmed). He married 佐波遲比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 沙本毘古命 (reading unconfirmed), and 品牟都和氣命 (reading unconfirmed) was born; counting the children of his other consorts as well, he had sixteen princes and princesses. Of these, 大帶日子淤斯呂和氣命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm, and 印色入日子命 (reading unconfirmed) made the 血沼 Pond, the 狹山 Pond and the 高津 Pond of 日下 (reading unconfirmed), and had a thousand swords made at the 河上宮 of 鳥取 (reading unconfirmed) and dedicated them to Isonokami Shrine (石上神宮). Small-script notes also record that 倭比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped and served the Great Shrine of Ise (伊勢大神宮), and that 布多遲能伊理毘賣命 (reading unconfirmed) became the consort of Yamato Takeru (倭建命).

While the emperor had 沙本毘賣 (reading unconfirmed) as his consort, her elder brother 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed) asked his sister, "Whom do you love more, your husband or your brother?", and the consort answered, "I love my brother." 沙本毘古王 then plotted, saying, "If you truly love me, let you and me rule the realm together." He had a cord dagger, the 八鹽折之紐小刀 (reading unconfirmed), made and gave it to his sister, ordering her to stab the emperor to death with it while he slept. The emperor, knowing nothing of the plot, fell asleep with his head on the consort's lap. Three times the consort raised the cord dagger to stab the emperor in the neck, but she could not bear her grief and could not stab him, and her tears fell onto the emperor's face.

The emperor woke with a start and asked the consort, "I dreamed that a sudden shower came from the direction of 沙本 (reading unconfirmed) and wet my face, and that a small brocade-colored snake coiled around my neck. What does this signify?" The consort, thinking she could not evade the question, told him everything: that when her brother asked her she had answered "I love my brother," that she had been handed a cord dagger to kill the emperor, and that though she raised it three times she could not stab him, and her tears fell.

The emperor said, "I was nearly deceived," and raised an army, and 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed) built a rice fortress (稻城) and met him in battle. The consort could not abandon her brother; she slipped out by the back gate and entered the rice fortress. At this time the consort was with child, and because she was pregnant and because he had loved and cherished her for three years, the emperor merely surrounded the fortress with his army and did not press the attack. Meanwhile the child was born, and the consort had the child placed outside the rice fortress and sent word that, if the emperor regarded it as his own child, he should take it and raise it.

Though the emperor resented her brother, he could not suppress his love for the consort. He chose strong and nimble soldiers and ordered them, when they received the child, to seize the mother too, by her hair or by her hands, and drag her out. Foreseeing this, the consort shaved off all her hair and covered her head with it, let her jewel cords rot and wound them three times around her hands, and rotted her clothes with sake so that they looked like ordinary clothes. The soldiers were able to receive the child, but when they grasped her hair it came away, when they grasped her hands the jewel cords broke, and when they grasped her clothes the clothes tore, so they could not bring the mother back. The emperor, full of regret, hated the people who had made the jewels and took away all their land, and it is said that from this arose the proverb "不得地玉作" (reading unconfirmed).

When the emperor asked the child's name, the consort answered that, since he was born in the fire at the very time the rice fortress was burning, it would be fitting to name him 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed). Asked how he should be raised, she answered that he should be brought up by appointing a 大湯坐 and a 若湯坐 (reading unconfirmed); and asked who would untie the 美豆能小佩 (reading unconfirmed) that she had tied, she answered that 兄比賣 and 弟比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughters of 旦波比古多多須美智宇斯王 (reading unconfirmed), would be suitable. Then the emperor at last killed 沙本比古王 (reading unconfirmed), and the consort, his younger sister, followed her brother in death.

quotes.note: Her brother asked, "Whom do you love more, your husband or your brother?", and the consort answered, "I love my brother."
The dream the emperor had: a sudden shower came from the direction of 沙本 (reading unconfirmed) and wet his face, and a small brocade-colored snake coiled around his neck.
The consort's answer that, since he was born in the fire, it would be fitting to name the child 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 伊久米伊理毘古伊佐知命 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Suinin)
figures.role: The emperor of this story. He learned of the rebellion through the consort's confession and struck down 沙本毘古王.

figures.name: 沙本毘古王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The consort's elder brother. He proposed to his sister that she assassinate the emperor; when the plot was exposed he shut himself in a rice fortress, fought, and was killed.

figures.name: 沙本毘賣命 (佐波遲比賣命) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Consort of Emperor Suinin. Torn between her brother and her husband, she handed the child over to the emperor and died together with her brother.

figures.name: 本牟智和氣御子 (品牟都和氣命) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The child born amid the fire of the rice fortress. The protagonist of the next story.

figures.name: The cord dagger (八鹽折之紐小刀) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The small dagger that 沙本毘古王 had made and handed to the consort so that she would stab the emperor.

figures.name: Rice fortress (稻城)
figures.role: The fortress 沙本毘古王 built for the battle. The consort entered it and gave birth to the child there.

figures.name: 兄比賣 and 弟比賣 (daughters of 旦波比古多多須美智宇斯王) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The sisters whom the consort recommended to serve the emperor in her place.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 6 — the 4th year of Emperor Suinin, autumn, 9th month (丙戌朔戊申)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the question of 狹穗彦王 (reading unconfirmed) is "Whom do you love more, your brother or your husband?" He further argues that one who serves others with beauty loses favor as that beauty fades, and gives her a dagger (匕首) to stab the emperor. The empress hides it in her clothing.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 6 — the 5th year of Emperor Suinin, winter, 10th month (己卯朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the emperor has 八綱田 (reading unconfirmed), distant ancestor of the 上毛野君 (reading unconfirmed), attack 狹穗彦 (reading unconfirmed), and 狹穗彦 builds a rice fortress by piling up rice. In the end 八綱田 sets fire to the fortress; the empress, holding the prince, carries him over the fortress wall and sends him out, and then dies inside the fortress together with her brother. The Kojiki's episode of escaping the soldiers' hands by means of tricks with her hair, jewel cords and clothes, and the exchange about naming the child, do not appear in this entry.

homuchiwake.title: Prince 本牟智和気御子 (reading unconfirmed) and 多遅摩毛理 (reading unconfirmed)
homuchiwake.lead: Prince 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed), who did not speak even when his long beard had grown down to his chest, was found to be under a curse of the Great Deity of Izumo (出雲大神); he went to worship at Izumo and, on the way back, spoke for the first time. At the end of the reign of Emperor Suinin, 多遲摩毛理 (reading unconfirmed) brought back the "登岐士玖能迦玖能木實" (reading unconfirmed) (the present-day tachibana, 橘) from the Eternal Land (常世國), but the emperor had already died.

points.text: Prince 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed) did not speak even when his eight-fist-long beard reached his chest. Through the emperor's dream and the great divination (太占) it was found that this was a curse arising from the will of the Great Deity of Izumo, so the prince was sent to worship the Great Deity at Izumo.

On the way back from worshipping at Izumo, on the bank of the 肥河 (reading unconfirmed), the prince saw the leafy green "mountain" decoration set up by 岐比佐都美 (reading unconfirmed) and spoke for the first time. The emperor rejoiced and had 菟上王 (reading unconfirmed) build the shrine of the deity at Izumo.

山邊之大鶙 (reading unconfirmed) pursued a swan (鵠) through many provinces, from 木國 to 高志國 (reading unconfirmed), caught it at 和那美之水門 (reading unconfirmed) and presented it, but even on seeing the bird the prince still did not speak.

多遲麻毛理 (reading unconfirmed) brought back the "登岐士玖能迦玖能木實" (reading unconfirmed) from the Eternal Land (常世國), but the emperor had already died, and he wept and wailed before the imperial tomb and died. The Kojiki records that this fruit is the present-day tachibana (橘).

In the Nihon Shoki (the 23rd year of Emperor Suinin), 譽津別命 (reading unconfirmed) sees a swan and says "是何物耶"; he is said to have gained speech by playing with the swan that 天湯河板擧 (reading unconfirmed) caught and presented. The curse of the Great Deity of Izumo and the pilgrimage to Izumo are not told.

The Kokugakuin University deity-name database treats the Great Deity of Izumo in this story as another name of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami (大国主神), and treats 葦原色許男大神 (reading unconfirmed), which appears in the prince's words, as a name of the same deity. It then introduces the view that the whole story, including the night with 肥長比賣 (reading unconfirmed), is connected with the rituals of Izumo, and a theory that sees it as a story telling how the problem of the worship of the Izumo deity was resolved.

story.text: The emperor had a two-hulled small boat (二俣小舟) made from a forked 榲 tree that stood at 相津 in Owari (reading unconfirmed), floated it on the 市師 Pond and the 輕 Pond in Yamato (reading unconfirmed), and let the prince play in it. But this prince still did not speak, even when his eight-fist-long beard reached down in front of his chest. One day, hearing the cry of a swan (鵠) flying high in the sky, the prince for the first time made "阿藝登比" (reading unconfirmed). The emperor therefore sent a man named 山邊之大鶙 (reading unconfirmed) to catch that bird.

大鶙 (reading unconfirmed) pursued the swan from 木國 to 針間國 (reading unconfirmed), then over 稻羽國 to 旦波國 and 多遲麻國 (reading unconfirmed), and, circling east, over Ōmi (近淡海國) and 三野國 (reading unconfirmed), and from Owari (尾張國) to 科野國 (reading unconfirmed). At last he spread a net at 和那美之水門 in 高志國 (reading unconfirmed), caught the bird, and brought it back to the capital to present it. But even on seeing the bird, the prince did not speak as the emperor had hoped.

When the emperor fell asleep troubled, he was told in a dream, "If you put my shrine in order like the emperor's palace (御舍), the prince will surely come to speak." When he sought through the great divination (太占) which deity's will this was, it was a curse arising from the will of the Great Deity of Izumo. 曙立王 (reading unconfirmed) was chosen by divination to accompany the prince; through ukehi-style oath divination (宇氣比), 曙立王 made a heron in a tree by the 鷺巣 Pond fall dead and then come back to life, and made a broad-leaved 熊白檮 oak in front of the 甜白檮 (reading unconfirmed) wither and then come back to life. The emperor gave 曙立王 the name "倭者師木登美豐朝倉曙立王" (reading unconfirmed).

曙立王 and 菟上王 (reading unconfirmed) set out accompanying the prince. Divination showed that from both the 那良戸 and the 大坂戸 (reading unconfirmed) gates they would meet the lame or the blind, and that only the 木戸 (reading unconfirmed) gate was auspicious, so they left by it, establishing 品遲部 (reading unconfirmed) groups wherever they went. After arriving in Izumo and finishing their worship of the Great Deity, on the way back they built the 黒巣 Bridge (reading unconfirmed) in the 肥河 river and a temporary palace, and lodged the prince there. When 岐比佐都美 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the governors of Izumo (出雲國造), set up downstream a decoration like a mountain of green leaves and was about to offer a meal, the prince said, "That thing downstream like a mountain of green leaves looks like a mountain but is not a mountain. Is it not the great ritual ground of the priests (祝) who worship 葦原色許男大神 (reading unconfirmed) in Izumo?"

The princes accompanying him rejoiced on hearing this, moved the prince to the 檳榔之長穂宮 (reading unconfirmed), and sent a fast-horse messenger to the capital. The prince spent one night with 肥長比賣 (reading unconfirmed), but when he secretly peeped, that beautiful person was a snake, and he fled in fear. As 肥長比賣 pursued him by boat, lighting up the sea, the prince grew even more afraid, hauled his boat over "山多和" (reading unconfirmed) and fled up to the capital. The princes reported, "Because he worshipped the Great Deity, the prince has spoken," and the emperor rejoiced, sent 菟上王 back to Izumo to build the shrine, and for the prince established the 鳥取部, 鳥甘部, 品遲部, 大湯坐 and 若湯坐 (reading unconfirmed).

In accordance with the words of his former consort, the emperor summoned four daughters of 美知能宇斯王 (reading unconfirmed): 比婆須比賣命, 弟比賣命, 歌凝比賣命 and 圓野比賣命 (reading unconfirmed). But he kept only two of them, 比婆須比賣命 and 弟比賣命, and sent the other two back to their home province as very ugly. 圓野比賣 (reading unconfirmed), ashamed, tried to die by hanging herself from a tree branch at 相樂 in 山代國 (reading unconfirmed), so that place is called 懸木 (the present 相樂); and when she reached 弟國 she fell into a deep pool and died, so that place is called 墮國 (the present 弟國) (reading unconfirmed).

The emperor also sent 多遲麻毛理 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 三宅連 (reading unconfirmed) and others, to the Eternal Land (常世國) to seek the "登岐士玖能迦玖能木實" (reading unconfirmed). 多遲摩毛理 reached that land, picked the fruit, and brought back eight 縵 and eight 矛 (縵八縵, 矛八矛) (reading unconfirmed), but in the meantime the emperor had already died. 多遲摩毛理 presented four 縵 and four 矛 to the empress, offered the remaining four 縵 and four 矛 at the door of the emperor's tomb, and, holding up the fruit and weeping and wailing, reported that he had brought it; then, still weeping and wailing, he died. That fruit is the present-day tachibana (橘). The emperor died at the age of 153, and his tomb is in the 御立野 of 菅原 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: Even when his long beard reached down in front of his chest, he still did not speak.
The revelation in the emperor's dream: "If you put my shrine in order like the emperor's palace (御舍), the prince will surely come to speak."
The report of the accompanying princes: "Because he worshipped the Great Deity, the prince has spoken. Therefore we have returned."
The fruit that 多遲摩毛理 (reading unconfirmed) brought back from the Eternal Land (常世國) is the present-day tachibana (橘).

figures.name: 本牟智和氣御子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Emperor Suinin and 沙本毘賣命. He did not speak, but spoke for the first time on the way back from worshipping at Izumo.

figures.name: 山邊之大鶙 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The man who pursued the swan through many provinces and caught it at 和那美之水門 in 高志國.

figures.name: 曙立王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince chosen by divination who performed an oath divination (宇氣比) and accompanied the prince to Izumo.

figures.name: 菟上王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince who accompanied the prince and was later sent back to Izumo to build the shrine.

figures.name: 岐比佐都美 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the governors of Izumo (出雲國造). He decorated a mountain of green leaves and tried to offer a meal, which led the prince to speak.

figures.name: 肥長比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: She spent a night with the prince, but was really a snake, and pursued the fleeing prince by boat.

figures.name: 圓野比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ashamed at being sent back as ugly, she fell into a pool at 弟國 and died.

figures.name: 多遲麻毛理 (多遲摩毛理) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 三宅連 and others. He brought back fruit from the Eternal Land (常世國) and wept and wailed before the emperor's tomb until he died.

figures.name: 登岐士玖能迦玖能木實 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The fruit that 多遲麻毛理 sought in the Eternal Land. The original text records that it is the present-day tachibana (橘).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 6 — the 23rd year of Emperor Suinin, autumn, 9th month (丙寅朔丁卯)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 譽津別王 (reading unconfirmed) reached thirty years of age, and even with a beard eight hand-spans long he wept like a child and did not speak, so the emperor had his ministers deliberate on it.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 6 — the 23rd year of Emperor Suinin, 11th month (甲午朔乙未)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 天湯河板擧 (reading unconfirmed) pursues the swan, catches it in Izumo (or, according to an alternative statement (或曰), in Tajima) and presents it, and 譽津別命 (reading unconfirmed) gains speech by playing with the swan. For this service he is granted the title 鳥取造, and the 鳥取部, 鳥養部 and 譽津部 (reading unconfirmed) are established. The curse of the Great Deity of Izumo and the pilgrimage to Izumo are not written.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 6 — the 90th year of Emperor Suinin, spring, 2nd month (庚子朔) / the year after his death, spring, 3rd month (辛未朔壬午)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed) is sent to the Eternal Land (常世國) in the 2nd month of the 90th year of Emperor Suinin to seek the 非時香菓 (reading unconfirmed), and he returns with eight rods and eight strings (八竿八縵) in the 3rd month of the year after the emperor's death. 田道間守 wept and wailed facing the emperor's tomb and died. The Kojiki's statement that half was presented to the empress does not appear in this entry.

yamatotakeru-saisei.title: The Western Campaign of 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed) (熊曾建 (reading unconfirmed) and Izumo Takeru)
yamatotakeru-saisei.lead: 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed), son of Emperor Keikō (大帶日子淤斯呂和氣天皇 (reading unconfirmed)), came to be feared by his father after violently killing his elder brother 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed), and was sent to strike down the 熊曾建 (reading unconfirmed) brothers in the west. Disguised as a young girl, he slipped into their feast and killed the brothers, received the name "倭建" (Yamato Takeru) offered to him by 熊曾建, and on the way back also killed Izumo Takeru (出雲建) by deceit.

points.text: Ordered to "泥疑" (reading unconfirmed) his elder brother 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed), 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed) seized his brother in the privy, tore off his limbs, wrapped him in a straw mat (薦) and threw him away. The emperor feared his violent heart and sent him to subdue the 熊曾建 (reading unconfirmed) in the west.

Disguising himself as a young girl by putting on the robe and skirt (御衣御裳) of his aunt 倭比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), 小碓命 slipped into the 熊曾建 (reading unconfirmed) brothers' "御室樂" (reading unconfirmed) feast and stabbed the brothers with his sword.
