karu.title: Emperor Ingyō, Crown Prince 軽 and 軽大郎女 (readings unconfirmed)
karu.lead: 男浅津間若子宿禰命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ingyō) at first declined to take the throne on account of illness, but his illness was cured by an envoy from Silla (新良), and he corrected the confusion in clan names and titles. After the emperor’s death, the heir 木梨之軽太子 (reading unconfirmed) had relations with his full sister 軽大郎女 (reading unconfirmed), was abandoned by the people and exiled to the hot springs of Iyo (伊余湯), and he and 軽大郎女, who followed him, took their own lives together.

points.text: 男浅津間若子宿禰命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ingyō) once declined to take the throne because of a long illness, but at the earnest request of the chief consort and the ministers, he ruled the realm. The chief envoy 金波鎮漢紀武 (reading unconfirmed), sent by the ruler of Silla (新良), cured the emperor’s illness with his knowledge of medicine.

Troubled by the confusion in clan names and titles (氏姓), the emperor set up 玖訶瓮 vessels (reading unconfirmed) at 言八十禍津日前 in 味白檮 (readings unconfirmed) and fixed the clan names and titles of the many hereditary groups (八十友緒) of the realm.

After the emperor’s death, 木梨之軽太子 (reading unconfirmed), who had been designated heir (日継), had relations with his full sister 軽大郎女 (reading unconfirmed) before his accession, so the officials and the people of the realm turned against him and went over to his younger brother, 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed).

Crown Prince 軽 fled to the house of 大前小前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), but the 宿禰 seized him and handed him over to 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed), and he was exiled to the hot springs of Iyo (伊余湯). 軽大郎女 (衣通王) (readings unconfirmed), unable to bear her longing, followed him, and the two took their own lives together. Their songs are recorded under names such as 志良宜歌, 天田振 and 読歌 (readings unconfirmed).

In the Nihon Shoki, the affair of the crown prince and 軽大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed) is placed in the lifetime of his father, Emperor Ingyō (the 23rd and 24th years); it is the princess who is exiled to Iyo, and the crown prince is not punished because he is the heir apparent. The crown prince later takes his own life at the house of 大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and it is also recorded, as one account, that he was exiled to Iyo Province. In addition, “衣通郎姫” (reading unconfirmed) in the Nihon Shoki is the name by which 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed), the empress’s younger sister, was known.

Kokugakuin University’s database of deity names notes that, because 言八十禍津日前 (written 辞禍戸岬 in the Nihon Shoki; readings unconfirmed) is a place name resembling the deity name 八十禍津日神 (reading unconfirmed), there is also a conjecture, though indirect, that the Magatsuhi deities are connected with kukatachi (盟神探湯), the ordeal for judging whether words are true or false.

story.text: 男浅津間若子宿禰命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ingyō) ruled the realm from the Far Asuka palace (遠飛鳥宮). He married 忍坂之大中津比売命 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 意富本杼王 (reading unconfirmed), and nine children were born: 木梨之軽王, 長田大郎女, 境之黒日子王, 穴穂命, 軽大郎女, 八瓜之白日子王, 大長谷命, 橘大郎女 and 酒見郎女 (readings unconfirmed). A small note says that 軽大郎女’s other name was 衣通郎女 (reading unconfirmed), and that because the radiance of her body shone through her clothes, she bore the name 衣通王. Of the nine, 穴穂命 and 大長谷命 ruled the realm.

When the emperor was about to receive the succession (日継), he declined, saying, “I have a long illness, so I cannot receive the succession.” But because the chief consort and the ministers urged him strongly, he ruled the realm. At this time the ruler of Silla (新良) sent eighty-one ships of tribute, and their chief envoy, 金波鎮漢紀武 (reading unconfirmed), knew the methods of medicine well and cured the emperor’s illness.

Troubled that the clan names and titles (氏姓) of the people of the various clans and names of the realm were in confusion, the emperor set up 玖訶瓮 vessels (reading unconfirmed) at 言八十禍津日前 in 味白檮 (readings unconfirmed) and fixed the clan names and titles of the many hereditary groups (八十友緒) of the realm. He also established the 軽部 as the namesake group (御名代) of 木梨之軽太子, the 刑部 as the namesake group of the chief consort, and the 河部 as the namesake group of the chief consort’s younger sister 田井中比売 (readings unconfirmed). The emperor lived to the age of seventy-eight, and his tomb is at 長枝 in 恵賀, Kawachi (readings unconfirmed).

After the emperor died, it was settled that 木梨之軽太子 (reading unconfirmed) would receive the succession. But before his accession he had relations with his full sister 軽大郎女 (reading unconfirmed) and sang songs (志良宜歌 and 夷振之上歌; readings unconfirmed). For this reason the officials and the people of the realm turned against Crown Prince 軽 and went over to 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed). Crown Prince 軽 took fright, fled into the house of the minister 大前小前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and prepared weapons. A small note says that the arrows made at this time had copper on the inner part of the arrow and were called “軽箭”, and that 穴穂御子 also made weapons, and those arrows are the arrows of today, called “穴穂箭” (readings unconfirmed).

穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed) raised an army and surrounded the house of 大前小前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed). When he reached the gate, a heavy icy rain fell, and 穴穂御子 sang a song. 大前小前宿禰 came out raising his hands and striking his knees, dancing and singing (宮人振; reading unconfirmed), and said, “Do not turn your troops against your royal brother born of the same mother. If you do, people will surely laugh at you. I will seize him and hand him over.” When 穴穂御子 withdrew his troops, 大前小前宿禰 seized Crown Prince 軽 and handed him over. The captured crown prince sang two songs.

Crown Prince 軽 was exiled to the hot springs of Iyo (伊余湯). As he was about to be sent away, the crown prince again sang songs (天田振 and 夷振之片下; readings unconfirmed). 衣通王 (軽大郎女) (readings unconfirmed) also offered a song.

Later, 衣通王 (reading unconfirmed), unable to bear her longing, followed after the crown prince and sang a song. When she caught up with him, the crown prince, who had been waiting for her, sang two songs (読歌; reading unconfirmed). Having finished singing in this way, the two took their own lives together.

quotes.note: I have a long illness, so I cannot receive the succession (the emperor’s words).
(The officials and the people of the realm) turned against Crown Prince 軽 and went over to 穴穂御子 (readings unconfirmed).
Thus Crown Prince 軽 (reading unconfirmed) was exiled to the hot springs of Iyo (伊余湯).
Having sung in this way, the two took their own lives together.

figures.name: 男淺津間若子宿禰命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Emperor Ingyō. He declined the throne on account of illness but took it, and fixed the clan names and titles. He lived to the age of seventy-eight.

figures.name: 忍坂之大中津比賣命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 意富本杼王 (reading unconfirmed) and chief consort. She bore nine children. The 刑部 was established as her namesake group (御名代).

figures.name: 金波鎭漢紀武 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Chief envoy of the tribute from Silla (新良). Versed in the methods of medicine, he cured the emperor’s illness.

figures.name: 木梨之輕太子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Ingyō, designated heir, but he had relations with his full sister, was abandoned by the people, and was exiled to the hot springs of Iyo (伊余湯).

figures.name: 輕大郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Ingyō. Her other name was 衣通郎女 (衣通王) (readings unconfirmed). She followed her brother, Crown Prince 軽, and died with him.

figures.name: 穴穂命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Ingyō (穴穂御子). Supported by the people, he later ruled the realm.

figures.name: 大前小前宿禰大臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Master of the house where Crown Prince 軽 took refuge. He seized the crown prince and handed him over to 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 玖訶瓮 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The vessel set up at 言八十禍津日前 in 味白檮 (readings unconfirmed) in order to fix the clan names and titles.

figures.name: 輕箭 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Arrows made on Crown Prince 軽’s side, with copper on the inner part of the arrow.

figures.name: 穴穂箭 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Arrows made on 穴穂御子’s side. A small note calls them “the arrows of today”.

figures.name: 伊余湯 (hot springs of Iyo)
figures.role: The place to which Crown Prince 軽 (reading unconfirmed) was exiled.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 13, the 7th year of Emperor Ingyō, winter, 12th month (壬戌朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, “衣通郎姫” (reading unconfirmed) is the name by which 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed), the empress’s younger sister, was known, given because her beauty shone through her clothes. In the Kojiki, 衣通郎女 (衣通王) is another name of 軽大郎女 (readings unconfirmed), so the names refer to different people.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 13, the 24th year of Emperor Ingyō, summer, 6th month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, in the 6th month of the 24th year, the soup for the emperor’s meal froze, divination pointed to internal disorder, and the affair of the crown prince and his full sister came to light. The crown prince was not punished because he was the heir apparent, and 軽大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed) was exiled to Iyo. In the Kojiki, this happens after the father’s death, and it is the crown prince who is exiled.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 13, Emperor Ankō, record before accession (the 42nd year of Emperor Ingyō)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, after Emperor Ingyō’s death, the crown prince takes refuge in the house of 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and the 宿禰 begs Prince 穴穂 (穴穂皇子; reading unconfirmed) not to harm the crown prince, but the crown prince takes his own life in that house; as one account, it is said that he was exiled to Iyo Province.

anko.title: Emperor Ankō and the Incident of 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed)
anko.lead: Emperor Ankō (穴穂御子; reading unconfirmed), believing the slander of his messenger 根臣 (reading unconfirmed), killed 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) and made his wife empress, but he was cut down during an afternoon nap by 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed), the empress’s son by her former husband. The emperor’s younger brother 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed) attacked his elder brothers and 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed), and then shot dead 市辺之忍歯王 (reading unconfirmed), so 忍歯王’s sons 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed) fled to Harima Province (針間国).

points.text: The seven-year-old 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed) overheard words saying that it was Emperor Ankō who had killed his father, 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed); he cut off the head of the napping emperor with a sword lying nearby and fled to the house of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that the emperor died at the age of fifty-six.

The affair began with the theft and slander of the messenger 根臣 (reading unconfirmed). 根臣 stole the jewelled headdress (玉縵) that was a gift of courtesy and falsely reported that 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) would not obey the command, so the emperor killed 大日下王 and made his wife, 長田大郎女 (reading unconfirmed), empress.

大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed; later Emperor Yūryaku) cut down his elder brother 黒日子王 (reading unconfirmed), who was not shocked by the incident, buried his other elder brother 白日子王 (reading unconfirmed) alive, and attacked the house of 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed), who was sheltering 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed). 意美 stabbed 目弱王 and then died himself.

During a hunt at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed), 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed) shot dead 市辺之忍歯王 (reading unconfirmed), and the latter’s sons 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed) hid in the house of 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima Province (針間国) and became keepers of horses and oxen.

In the Nihon Shoki, after a drinking party in a tall pavilion, Emperor Ankō is lying asleep drunk with his head on the empress’s lap when he is stabbed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed; corresponding to 目弱王), and 眉輪王 is burned to death in the minister’s house together with Prince 坂合黒彦 (坂合黒彦皇子) and the minister 円 (円大臣) (readings unconfirmed).

In the Nihon Shoki, 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed; Yūryaku) killed Prince 市辺押磐 (市辺押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed) because he resented the fact that Emperor Ankō had intended to pass the country to 押磐皇子, and it records that he shot him dead after falsely saying, “There is a boar.”

story.text: 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm from the 穴穂宮 palace at Isonokami (石上). Seeking to obtain 若日下王 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed), as a wife for his younger brother 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor sent 根臣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 坂本臣 (reading unconfirmed) and others, as his messenger. 大日下王 bowed four times and consented, and entrusted him with the jewelled headdress 押木之玉縵 (reading unconfirmed) as a gift of courtesy. But 根臣 stole the headdress and falsely told the emperor that 大日下王 had refused the command and was angry.

The emperor was greatly enraged and killed 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed), and made his principal wife, 長田大郎女 (reading unconfirmed), empress. Once, while taking an afternoon nap on a sacred couch (神牀), the emperor told the empress that he was always anxious that when her son 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed) grew up and learned that it was he who had killed his father, he might turn against him. The seven-year-old 目弱王, playing beneath the palace, heard this; he took the sword lying beside the sleeping emperor, cut off his head, and fled into the house of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that the emperor lived to the age of fifty-six and that his tomb is at 伏見岡 in 菅原 (readings unconfirmed).

大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed), who was still a boy, was furious when he heard this and went to his elder brother 黒日子王 (reading unconfirmed), but 黒日子王 was not shocked and seemed indifferent. 大長谷王子 reviled his brother, seized him by the collar, dragged him out and cut him down. His next elder brother, 白日子王 (reading unconfirmed), behaved the same way, so he took him to 小治田 (reading unconfirmed), dug a pit and buried him standing; it is recorded that when he had been buried to the waist, both his eyes burst out and he died.

大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed) raised an army, surrounded the house of 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed), and the two sides shot arrows fiercely at each other. 意美 laid down his weapons, bowed eight times, and said he would offer his daughter 訶良比売 (reading unconfirmed), whom the prince had earlier sought, together with five granaries (屯宅). But, saying that he had heard of ministers hiding in royal palaces but never of a prince hiding in a minister’s house, and that he would not abandon a prince who had come to rely on him even if it meant death, he fought again. When his strength and arrows were exhausted, he followed the prince’s words, stabbed the prince to death, and then cut his own throat and died.

After that, 韓帒 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 佐佐紀山君 (reading unconfirmed) of Ōmi, reported that there were many boar and deer at 蚊屋野 in 久多綿 (readings unconfirmed), and 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed) went to Ōmi taking 市辺之忍歯王 (reading unconfirmed) with him; each stayed in his own temporary lodging. The next morning, 忍歯王, quite unguarded, rode up on horseback beside 大長谷王’s lodging and invited him to the hunting ground. Because his attendants urged him to be on his guard, 大長谷王 went out wearing armour under his clothes, and as soon as their horses were side by side he shot 忍歯王 down with an arrow, cut up his body, put it in a horse’s feeding trough, and buried it level with the ground.

The sons of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed), 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed), heard of this disturbance and fled. While they were eating at 苅羽井 in Yamashiro (山代) (reading unconfirmed), an old man with a tattooed face came and took their food, naming himself the boar-keeper (猪甘) of Yamashiro. The two crossed the 玖須婆 river (reading unconfirmed), reached Harima Province (針間国), hid themselves in the house of a man named 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed), and worked as keepers of horses and oxen.

quotes.note: 根臣 (reading unconfirmed) stole the jewelled headdress, the gift of courtesy entrusted to him by 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed).
目弱王 (reading unconfirmed) took the sword lying beside the sleeping emperor and cut off the emperor’s head.
The words of 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed): I have heard of ministers fleeing into royal palaces, but I have never heard of a prince hiding in a minister’s house.
The two sons of 市辺王, 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed), heard of this disturbance and fled.

figures.name: 穴穂御子 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ankō)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 穴穂宮 palace at Isonokami (石上). He kills 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) and is cut down by 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大長谷王子, also 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger brother of Emperor Ankō. On hearing of his brother’s death, he brings down 黒日子王, 白日子王 and 都夫良意美 (readings unconfirmed), and shoots dead 市辺之忍歯王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 根臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 坂本臣 (reading unconfirmed) and others. As messenger, he steals the jewelled headdress entrusted to him and makes false reports about 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of 若日下王 (reading unconfirmed). He agreed to give his sister in marriage, but is killed because of slander.

figures.name: 若日下王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed). She is sought as a wife for 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 押木之玉縵 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The jewelled headdress that 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) entrusted as a gift of courtesy for his sister. It is stolen by 根臣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 長田大郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Principal wife of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed). After his death she is made empress of Emperor Ankō. Mother of 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 長田大郎女 (reading unconfirmed). At the age of seven he overhears the emperor’s words, cuts the emperor down, and flees to the house of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 都夫良意富美, also 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He shelters 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed) and, after fighting the army of 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed), stabs 目弱王 and kills himself.

figures.name: 訶良比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed). Named as the woman whom 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed) had sought.

figures.name: 黑日子王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed). He is cut down because he was not shocked by the incident.

figures.name: 白日子王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of 大長谷王子 (reading unconfirmed). He is buried alive at 小治田 (reading unconfirmed) and dies.

figures.name: 韓帒 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 佐佐紀山君 (reading unconfirmed) of Ōmi. He reports that there are many boar and deer at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 市邊之忍齒王, also 市邊王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Invited to a hunt by 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed), he is shot dead at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed). Father of 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 意富祁王 and 袁祁王 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sons of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed). Escaping the disturbance, they hide in the house of 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima Province (針間国) and become keepers of horses and oxen.

figures.name: 山代之猪甘 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An old man with a tattooed face. He takes the food of the two fleeing princes.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 13, the 1st year of Emperor Ankō, spring, 2nd month (戊辰朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki too, 根使主 (reading unconfirmed; corresponding to 根臣) is captivated by the beauty of the jewelled headdress 押木珠縵 (reading unconfirmed), keeps it for himself, and through slander has 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed; corresponding to 大日下王) killed. The Nihon Shoki further records that 難波吉師日香蛟 (reading unconfirmed) and his sons, who had served 大草香皇子, killed themselves beside their master’s body.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, Emperor Yūryaku, record before accession (the 3rd year of Emperor Ankō, 8th month)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, after holding a drinking party in the tall pavilion of the mountain palace (山宮), Emperor Ankō is taking an afternoon nap, drunk, with his head on the empress’s lap when he is stabbed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed). (In the Kojiki, he is napping on a sacred couch (神牀), and his head is cut off with a sword.)

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, Emperor Yūryaku, record before accession (the 3rd year of Emperor Ankō, 8th month)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Prince 八釣白彦 (八釣白彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) is cut down, and Prince 坂合黒彦 (坂合黒彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) flees with 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed) to the house of the minister 円 (円大臣; reading unconfirmed); the minister offers his daughter 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed) and seven residences in Katsuragi (葛城) and begs for pardon, but he is not forgiven, and all three are burned to death together with the house. This differs from the Kojiki’s accounts of 白日子王 (reading unconfirmed) being buried alive and of 意美 (reading unconfirmed) stabbing the prince and killing himself.

yuryaku-akaiko.title: Emperor Yūryaku with 若日下部王, 赤猪子 and the Maiden of Yoshino (readings unconfirmed)
yuryaku-akaiko.lead: The first half of the section on Emperor Yūryaku (大長谷若建命; reading unconfirmed) tells of his courtship of 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed) and the white dog; of 引田部赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed), who waited eighty years for the emperor’s word; of the dance of the maiden of Yoshino; and of the origin of the name 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed). Each story is accompanied by songs of the emperor or of the woman concerned.

points.text: 引田部赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed) waited eighty years for the emperor’s words, “I will send for you in time,” but the emperor had forgotten them completely. The emperor was astonished and pitied her, but, held back by her great age, he did not marry her; he gave her songs and many gifts and sent her home.

The great district chief (大県主) of 志幾 (reading unconfirmed) raised katsuogi ridge-logs (堅魚木) on his roof in imitation of the emperor’s palace, so his house was nearly burned; he was pardoned after presenting a white dog. The emperor made that dog his courtship gift to 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed).
The origin of the name 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed): during a hunt, a horsefly that had bitten the emperor’s arm was eaten by a dragonfly (蜻蛉, akizu), so that field was called 阿岐豆野.
The emperor, who married a maiden he met on the bank of the Yoshino River, later played the koto at the same place and had that maiden dance, and he composed a song about her dance.

The Nihon Shoki also has a story of a dragonfly eating a horsefly (the 4th year, autumn, 8th month), but it places the event in the 河上小野 field (reading unconfirmed) after a visit to the Yoshino palace, and says that the emperor tried to have his ministers compose a song praising the dragonfly, but no one could, so the emperor sang one himself.

Genealogy: the emperor married 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed; there were no children) and 韓比売 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed), and from 韓比売 were born 白髪命 and 若帯比売命 (readings unconfirmed).

story.text: 大長谷若建命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm from the 朝倉宮 palace at 長谷 (readings unconfirmed). He married 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed), but they had no children; he also married 韓比売 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed), and 白髪命 and 若帯比売命 (readings unconfirmed) were born. As the namesake group (御名代) of Crown Prince 白髪 he established the 白髪部, and he also established the 長谷部舎人 and the 河瀬舎人 (readings unconfirmed). It is recorded that at this time people from 呉 (呉人; reading unconfirmed) came across the sea, and they were settled at 呉原 (reading unconfirmed), and that the place came to be called 呉原.

When 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed) was still living at 日下 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor went to Kawachi by the 直越 road of 日下 (readings unconfirmed). Looking out over the land from the top of the mountain, he saw a house with katsuogi ridge-logs (堅魚木) raised on its roof. Told that it was the house of the great district chief (大県主) of 志幾 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor grew angry that it had been built in imitation of his own palace and was about to have it burned. The chief, in fear, apologised and presented a white dog led on a cloth and hung with a bell, so the emperor had them stop setting the fire.

The emperor had the dog delivered to 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed) as a courtship gift, calling it a rare thing he had obtained on the road. 若日下部王 replied that, since his coming with the sun at his back was a matter for great awe, she would come to him herself and serve him. As the emperor returned to his palace, he stood at the top of the mountain slope and composed a song, which he sent back with the messenger.

Once, when the emperor went out to the banks of the 美和河 river (reading unconfirmed), there was a beautiful maiden washing clothes. When he asked her name, she answered 引田部赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor told her, “Do not marry a husband. I will send for you in time,” and returned to his palace. 赤猪子 kept waiting for those words until eighty years had passed and her looks had faded; but unable to keep from showing that she had waited, she came to the palace bringing many gifts. The emperor had completely forgotten his earlier words and asked what old woman she was and why she had come.

When 赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed) explained what had happened, the emperor was greatly astonished and deeply pitied her for having kept her resolve and let the years of her prime pass in vain. In his heart he wished to marry her, but held back by her very great age, he did not do so, and sent her two songs. 赤猪子 wept until the sleeves of her red-dyed (丹摺) garment were soaked through, and answered with two songs. The emperor gave her many gifts and sent her home; it is recorded that these four songs are 志都歌 (reading unconfirmed).

When the emperor went to the Yoshino palace, there was a maiden of beautiful appearance on the bank of the Yoshino River, so he married her and returned to his palace. Later, when he went to Yoshino again, he stopped at the place where he had met the maiden, sat on his great seat (大御呉床), played the koto and had the maiden dance. Because her dance was so fine, the emperor composed a song.

Next, while he was hunting at 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed), a horsefly bit the arm of the emperor as he sat on his seat (呉床), and a dragonfly (蜻蛉, akizu) flew up, ate the horsefly and flew away. The emperor composed a song about this, and it is said that from that time the field has been called 阿岐豆野.

quotes.note: The emperor’s words to 赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed): Do not marry a husband; I will send for you in time.
赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed) kept waiting for the emperor’s words, and eighty years had already passed.
On hearing the emperor’s songs, 赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed) wept until the sleeves of the red-dyed (丹摺) garment she wore were soaked through.
From this time that field came to be called 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大長谷若建命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Yūryaku)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 朝倉宮 palace at 長谷 (readings unconfirmed). He courts 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed) and sends songs to 赤猪子 and the maiden of Yoshino.

figures.name: 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) and wife of the emperor. She is sent a white dog and replies that she will come to him herself.

figures.name: 韓比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 都夫良意富美 (reading unconfirmed). She bears 白髪命 and 若帯比売命 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 白髮命, also 白髮太子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of the emperor and 韓比売 (reading unconfirmed). The 白髪部 is established as his namesake group (御名代).

figures.name: 呉人 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: People who came across the sea and were settled at 呉原 (reading unconfirmed). Regarded as the origin of the place name “呉原”.

figures.name: 志幾之大縣主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Rebuked for building his house in imitation of the emperor’s palace, he is pardoned after presenting a white dog.

figures.name: White dog (白犬)
figures.role: A dog presented led on a cloth and hung with a bell. It becomes the courtship gift to 若日下部王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 引田部赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A maiden who was washing clothes at the 美和河 river (reading unconfirmed). She waits eighty years for the emperor’s word and comes to the palace as an old woman.

figures.name: The maiden of Yoshino (original text: “童女”)
figures.role: She meets the emperor on the bank of the Yoshino River and marries him, and later dances to the emperor’s koto.

figures.name: Great seat (大御呉床, also 呉床)
figures.role: The seat on which the emperor sat at Yoshino and at 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Akizu, dragonfly (蜻蛉)
figures.role: The insect that ate the horsefly that had bitten the emperor’s arm. It is the origin of the name 阿岐豆野 (reading unconfirmed) (reading note: “訓蜻蛉云阿岐豆”).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, the 1st year of Emperor Yūryaku, 3rd month, this month
compare.text: The Nihon Shoki also says that 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the minister 葛城円 (葛城円大臣; reading unconfirmed), bore Prince 白髪 (白髪皇子; reading unconfirmed; Emperor Seinei) and Princess 稚足姫 (稚足姫皇女; reading unconfirmed), which agrees with the Kojiki; but the Nihon Shoki writes her father as “葛城円大臣”, and also lists 吉備稚媛 and 童女君 (readings unconfirmed) as consorts.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, the 4th year of Emperor Yūryaku, autumn, 8th month (庚戌)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, when the emperor was hunting in the 河上小野 field (reading unconfirmed) after a visit to the Yoshino palace, a horsefly bit the emperor’s arm, and a dragonfly carried the horsefly off in its mouth. The emperor tried to have his ministers compose a song praising the dragonfly, but no one could, so he sang one himself and named the place 蜻蛉野 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, the 14th year of Emperor Yūryaku, 3rd month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the reception of envoys from 呉 (reading unconfirmed), the settling of the 呉 people at 桧隈野 (reading unconfirmed), and the naming of that place 呉原 (reading unconfirmed) are placed in the 3rd month of the 14th year of Emperor Yūryaku. Entries corresponding to the stories of 赤猪子 (reading unconfirmed) and the maiden of Yoshino could not be confirmed in the Yūryaku chapter of the Nihon Shoki.

yuryaku-hitokoto.title: Hitokotonushi-no-Kami of Katsuragi and the Songs of Emperor Yūryaku
yuryaku-hitokoto.lead: On Mount Katsuragi, Emperor Yūryaku met a procession exactly like his own; learning that its master was Hitokotonushi-no-Kami of Katsuragi (葛城之一言主大神), he was filled with awe and presented swords, bows and arrows, and the clothing of his officials. This section also contains the emperor’s song when chased by a boar, the story of 袁杼比売 (reading unconfirmed) and the 金鉏岡 hill (reading unconfirmed), and the 天語歌 (reading unconfirmed) of the palace attendant from Mie, and it records that the emperor died at the age of one hundred and twenty-four.

points.text: On Mount Katsuragi he met a company with the same attire and the same number of people as the emperor’s, and when he asked its name, the other named himself “Hitokotonushi-no-Kami of Katsuragi (葛城之一言主大神)”. The emperor, filled with awe, presented swords, bows and arrows and the clothing of his officials, and the Great Deity escorted the emperor as far as the entrance to the mountains of 長谷 (reading unconfirmed).

In the Nihon Shoki (the 4th year of Emperor Yūryaku, spring, 2nd month), the deity 一事主神 (reading unconfirmed) appears as a “tall man” (長人) resembling the emperor, hunts side by side with the emperor and escorts him as far as 来目水 (reading unconfirmed), and the people are said to have called him “an emperor of virtue” (有徳天皇).

The palace attendant (婇) from Mie offered sake with a zelkova (槻) leaf still floating in the cup and was nearly beheaded, but she was pardoned for offering a song and was even given rewards. Her song and the songs of the chief consort and the emperor, three in all, are called 天語歌 (reading unconfirmed).

The reading and meaning of “言離之神”, the words with which Hitokotonushi describes himself, are disputed, with views such as kotosaka, ihihanatsu and kotohanatsu, and this is regarded as bearing heavily on the interpretation of the deity’s name.

Kokugakuin University’s database of deity names introduces the observation that, because in the Nihon Shoki the emperor refers to himself as “朕” and the deity refers to himself as “僕”, the Nihon Shoki portrays the emperor as the superior.
It is recorded that the emperor lived to the age of one hundred and twenty-four and that his tomb is at 多治比高鸇 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi.

story.text: Once, when the emperor climbed to the top of a mountain in Katsuragi, a great boar came out. When the emperor shot it with a whistling arrow (鳴鏑), the boar came at him in anger, “宇多岐” (reading unconfirmed); fearing it, the emperor climbed up into a hazel (榛) tree and composed a song.

Another time, when the emperor climbed Mount Katsuragi, all his officials wore blue-printed (青摺) robes with red cords. At that moment a company exactly like the emperor’s procession, in both attire and number, was climbing the ridge of the mountain opposite. When the emperor had them asked, “In this land of Yamato (倭) there is no king but me, so who goes along like this?”, the other side answered in the same words as the emperor. The emperor was greatly enraged and fitted an arrow to his bow, and when all his officials did the same, the people on the other side all fitted arrows too.

When the emperor said they should give their names, and each side was about to name itself and loose its arrows, the other answered that, since he had been asked first, he would name himself first: he was the deity who pronounces bad things with one word and good things with one word, Hitokotonushi-no-Kami of Katsuragi (葛城之一言主大神). The emperor was filled with awe and said that he had not recognised him because he was “宇都志意美” (reading unconfirmed), and he presented swords and bows and arrows and had his officials take off their clothing and offered it as well. Hitokotonushi clapped his hands and accepted the offerings, and when the emperor returned, escorted him as far as the entrance to the mountains of 長谷 (reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that this Hitokotonushi appeared at this time.

The emperor went to Kasuga (春日) intending to marry 袁杼比売 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 佐都紀臣 of 丸邇 (readings unconfirmed). When 袁杼比売 met the procession on the road, she ran off and hid beside a hill, so the emperor composed a song. For that reason the hill is called 金鉏岡 (reading unconfirmed).

When the emperor held a drinking party under the 百枝槻 zelkova (reading unconfirmed) at 長谷 (reading unconfirmed), the palace attendant (婇) from Mie in Ise Province held up the great sake cup, but offered the sake without noticing that a zelkova leaf had fallen and was floating in the cup. Seeing this, the emperor struck the attendant down, put his blade to her neck and was about to behead her, but she said, “Do not kill me. I have something to say,” and composed a song. Because she offered this song, her offence was pardoned, and then the chief consort and the emperor also composed songs. These three songs are called 天語歌 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor praised the attendant from Mie and gave her many gifts.

On the day of the same drinking party, when 袁杼比売 (reading unconfirmed) of Kasuga offered the great sake, the emperor sang (宇岐歌; reading unconfirmed), and 袁杼比売 also offered a song (志都歌; reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that the emperor lived to the age of one hundred and twenty-four and that his tomb is at 多治比高鸇 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi.

quotes.note: The emperor’s words: In this land of Yamato (倭) there is no king but me.
Hitokotonushi’s self-naming: I am the deity who pronounces bad things with one word and good things with one word, Hitokotonushi-no-Kami of Katsuragi (葛城之一言主大神).
Because the palace attendant from Mie offered this song, her offence was pardoned.
The emperor lived to the age of one hundred and twenty-four.

figures.name: The emperor (大長谷若建命 (reading unconfirmed), Emperor Yūryaku)
figures.role: On Mount Katsuragi he meets a boar and Hitokotonushi, and composes many songs.

figures.name: Great boar (大猪)
figures.role: Shot by the emperor on Mount Katsuragi, it comes at him in anger. The emperor escapes by climbing a hazel tree.

figures.name: Whistling arrow (鳴鏑)
figures.role: The sounding arrow with which the emperor shot the boar.

figures.name: The officials (百官人等)
figures.role: They attend the emperor in blue-printed robes with red cords, and are later made to present their clothing to Hitokotonushi.

figures.name: 袁杼比賣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 佐都紀臣 of 丸邇 (readings unconfirmed). She hides beside a hill on seeing the procession, and later offers a song at a drinking party.

figures.name: 金鉏岡 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The hill where 袁杼比売 (reading unconfirmed) hid. It is said to have been named after the emperor’s song.

figures.name: The palace attendant from Mie (三重婇)
figures.role: A palace attendant from Mie in Ise Province. Failing to notice a zelkova leaf floating in the cup, she is nearly beheaded, but is pardoned for her song.

figures.name: 百枝槻 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The zelkova tree at the site of the drinking party at 長谷 (reading unconfirmed). Its leaf falls into the cup.

figures.name: The chief consort (大后)
figures.role: She composes one of the 天語歌 (reading unconfirmed) songs at the drinking party.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, the 4th year of Emperor Yūryaku, spring, 2nd month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, while the emperor is hunting on Mount Katsuragi, a tall man resembling the emperor appears, names himself “一事主神” (reading unconfirmed), hunts together with the emperor, and at dusk escorts him as far as 来目水 (reading unconfirmed). There is no scene, as in the Kojiki, in which the emperor is filled with awe and presents clothing.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 14, the 5th year of Emperor Yūryaku, spring, 2nd month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki an enraged boar also appears on Mount Katsuragi, but the emperor stops it with his bow and tramples it to death, and it is an attendant (舎人) who climbs a tree to escape. A song closely resembling the one the emperor composes in the Kojiki is attributed to the attendant when he is about to be executed, and the attendant is pardoned at the empress’s remonstrance.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, the 1st year of Emperor Seinei, winter, 10th month (癸巳朔辛丑)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Yūryaku dies in the great hall in the 8th month of the 23rd year and is buried in the 丹比高鷲原 tomb (reading unconfirmed) in the 10th month, winter, of the 1st year of Emperor Seinei. The place name of the tomb corresponds to the Kojiki’s “多治比高鸇” (reading unconfirmed), but no figure for his age like the Kojiki’s “one hundred and twenty-four” appears in the Nihon Shoki’s entry on his death.

oke-woke.title: Emperor Seinei and 意祁命 and 袁祁命 (readings unconfirmed): the Song Gathering with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed)
oke-woke.lead: After Emperor Seinei (白髪大倭根子命; reading unconfirmed) died without children, the brothers 意祁命 and 袁祁命 (readings unconfirmed), sons of 市辺之押歯王 (reading unconfirmed) who had been hiding in Harima Province (針間国), revealed themselves at a house-warming banquet and were found. The younger brother, 袁祁命, exchanged songs with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed) at a song gathering (歌垣) and brought him down, and, at his elder brother’s yielding, he ruled the realm first.

points.text: At the house-warming banquet of 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima Province (針間国), the younger brother 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed), who had been working as a boy tending the fire, declared his identity while dancing, and it became known that they were sons of 押歯王 of 市辺 (readings unconfirmed). 山部連小楯 (reading unconfirmed), astonished, sheltered the two and sent word to the capital.

Emperor Seinei (白髪大倭根子命; reading unconfirmed) had neither empress nor children, and the 白髪部 (reading unconfirmed) was established as his namesake group (御名代). It is recorded that after his death there was no prince to succeed him, and that 飯豊王 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 市辺忍歯別王 (reading unconfirmed), was at the 高木角刺宮 palace at 忍海 in Katsuragi (readings unconfirmed).

At a song gathering (歌垣), 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) exchanged songs over 大魚 (reading unconfirmed) with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 平群臣 (reading unconfirmed); the next morning he consulted with his elder brother 意富祁命 (reading unconfirmed), raised an army and killed 志毘臣.

The elder brother, 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed), yielded the realm, saying it was his younger brother’s merit that he had revealed their names and shown their rank, and the younger brother, 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed), ruled the realm first.

In the Nihon Shoki, it is Emperor Buretsu in his time as crown prince who exchanges songs at a song gathering with 鮪 (reading unconfirmed), son of 平群真鳥 (reading unconfirmed), over a woman (影媛; reading unconfirmed), and a song closely resembling the one 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) composes in the Kojiki appears as the crown prince’s song.

story.text: 白髪大倭根子命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm from the 甕栗宮 palace at 伊波礼 (readings unconfirmed). Because he had neither empress nor children, he established the 白髪部 (reading unconfirmed) as his namesake group (御名代). When the emperor died there was no prince to rule the realm, so they searched for a prince to take up the succession (日継); it is recorded that 忍海郎女 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 市辺忍歯別王 (reading unconfirmed), also called 飯豊王 (reading unconfirmed), was at the 高木角刺宮 palace at 忍海 in Katsuragi (readings unconfirmed).

When 山部連小楯 (reading unconfirmed) was appointed governor of Harima Province (針間国), he went to the banquet celebrating the new house of a man of that province named 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed). As the banquet grew lively, everyone danced in turn, and the two boys who were tending the fire beside the hearth were also made to dance. The two deferred to each other, “You first, elder brother,” “You first, younger brother,” and the people laughed at them; but when the elder had finished dancing, the younger recited while dancing, declaring that they were descendants of 押歯王 of 市辺 (readings unconfirmed), child of Emperor 伊邪本和気 (伊邪本和気天皇; reading unconfirmed).

On hearing this, 小楯 (reading unconfirmed) was astonished and tumbled from his seat; he drove the people of the house outside, set the two princes on his left and right knees and wept. He gathered people, built a temporary palace, had the two live there, and sent a messenger by fast horse to the capital. Their aunt, 飯豊王 (reading unconfirmed), rejoiced at this and had the two come up to the palace.

Before the two had begun to rule the realm, 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 平群臣 (reading unconfirmed), stood at a song gathering (歌垣) and took the hand of 大魚 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the 菟田首 (reading unconfirmed) and others, whom 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) intended to marry. 袁祁命 also stood at the song gathering, and 志毘臣 and 袁祁命 exchanged songs in turn. It is recorded that as he sang, 志毘臣 grew more and more angry.

The two sang to each other until dawn and then each withdrew. The next morning 意富祁命 and 袁祁命 (readings unconfirmed) conferred: the people of the court come to the court in the morning but gather at 志毘’s gate at midday; now 志毘 will be asleep and there will be no one at his gate; if not now, it will be hard to carry out a plan. They then raised an army, surrounded the house of 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed) and killed him.

After that, the two princes each tried to yield the realm to the other. The elder brother, 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed), firmly yielded it, saying that if his younger brother had not revealed their names when they were in the house of 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima, they would never have become lords of the realm; this was his younger brother’s achievement, so although he himself was the elder, his younger brother should rule the realm first. For this reason 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) could not refuse, and he ruled the realm first.

quotes.note: The younger prince’s declaration: we are descendants (末) of 押歯王 of 市辺 (readings unconfirmed), child of Emperor 伊邪本和気 (reading unconfirmed).
On hearing the declaration, 小楯 (reading unconfirmed) was astonished and tumbled from his seat.
The words of the elder brother, 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed): although I am the elder, you should still rule the realm first; he yielded it firmly.

figures.name: 白髮大倭根子命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Seinei)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 甕栗宮 palace at 伊波礼 (readings unconfirmed). He had neither empress nor children, and after his death there was no heir.

figures.name: 飯豐王, also 忍海郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 市辺忍歯別王 (reading unconfirmed). She was at the 高木角刺宮 palace at 忍海 in Katsuragi (readings unconfirmed), and has the two princes, once found, come up to the palace.

figures.name: 山部連小楯 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Governor of Harima Province (針間国). He finds the two princes at the house-warming banquet of 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed) and sends word to the capital.

figures.name: 志自牟 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of Harima Province (針間国). The two princes hid and worked in his house, where the house-warming banquet is held.

figures.name: 意富祁命, also 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed) and the elder brother. He dances first at the house-warming banquet, and later yields the realm to his younger brother.

figures.name: 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed) and the younger brother. He declares his identity while dancing, exchanges songs with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed) at a song gathering, and rules the realm first.

figures.name: 市邊之押齒王, also 市邊忍齒別王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of the two princes. His name is mentioned in the younger brother’s declaration.

figures.name: 伊邪本和氣天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Mentioned in the younger brother’s declaration as the father of 押歯王 of 市辺 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 平群臣 (reading unconfirmed). At a song gathering he takes the hand of 大魚 (reading unconfirmed) and exchanges songs with 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed), but is struck down the next morning.

figures.name: 大魚 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the 菟田首 (reading unconfirmed) and others. The woman 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) intended to marry.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, the 2nd year of Emperor Seinei, winter, 11th month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, in the 11th month, winter, of the 2nd year of Emperor Seinei, the provincial governor of Harima (播磨国司), 伊予来目部小楯 (reading unconfirmed), finds 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed; corresponding to 意祁 and 袁祁) at the new house of the head of the 縮見 granary (縮見屯倉首), 忍海部造細目 (readings unconfirmed), in Akashi District (赤石郡). In the Kojiki, the master of the house is written “志自牟” (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, Emperor Kenzō, record before accession (the 5th year of Emperor Seinei)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 飯豊王 (reading unconfirmed) is the “younger sister” of 市辺忍歯別王 (reading unconfirmed), but in this entry of the Nihon Shoki she is 飯豊青皇女 (reading unconfirmed), the “elder sister” of Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed); after Emperor Seinei’s death, while the brothers were yielding the throne to each other, she conducted government at the 忍海角刺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and she died in the 11th month, winter, of the same year.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 16, Emperor Buretsu, record before accession
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, it is the crown prince (later Emperor Buretsu) who exchanges songs with 鮪 (reading unconfirmed) over 影媛 (reading unconfirmed) at the song place (歌場, a song gathering) of 海柘榴市 (reading unconfirmed), and a song closely resembling “志毘賀波多傳爾。都麻多弖理美由”, which the prince composes in the Kojiki, appears as the crown prince’s song.

kenzo.title: Emperor Kenzō and Emperor Ninken: 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed) and Their Father’s Tomb
kenzo.lead: Emperor Kenzō (袁祁之石巣別命; reading unconfirmed), guided by an old woman of Ōmi, found and buried the remains of his father, 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed); he gave the old woman the name 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed) and treated her generously. He tried to destroy the tomb of Emperor 大長谷 (大長谷天皇; reading unconfirmed), his father’s enemy, but his elder brother 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed) only dug a little at its side and remonstrated with him; after the emperor’s death, that elder brother (Emperor Ninken) ruled the realm.

points.text: Emperor Kenzō (袁祁之石巣別命; reading unconfirmed), on the offer of an old woman of Ōmi, found the remains of his father, 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed), built a tomb on the mountain east of 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed) and buried him there. The old woman was given the name 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed), lived beside the palace, and was summoned by a bell (鐸) hung at the door of the great hall.

The emperor tried to destroy the tomb of Emperor 大長谷 (大長谷天皇; reading unconfirmed), his father’s enemy, but his elder brother 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed) dug only a little at its side and remonstrated that he was their uncle and also an emperor who had ruled the realm. The emperor too acknowledged this as reasonable.

It is recorded that the old boar-keeper (猪甘) who had taken their food while they were fleeing was sought out and beheaded on the bank of the Asuka River (飛鳥河), and that the tendons of his kinsmen’s knees were cut.

Emperor Kenzō died at the age of thirty-eight (he reigned eight years, and his tomb is on 石坏岡 hill at 片岡; readings unconfirmed). He was followed by his elder brother 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ninken), who ruled the realm from the 広高宮 palace at Isonokami (石上) (reading unconfirmed), and Ninken’s child 小長谷若雀命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm next.

In the Nihon Shoki, the crown prince 億計 (reading unconfirmed) remonstrates with the emperor, who is trying to destroy the tomb, and the emperor has the work stopped; there is no story of digging a little at the side of the tomb.

story.text: 袁祁之石巣別命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm for eight years from the Near Asuka palace (近飛鳥宮). He married 難波王 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 石木王 (reading unconfirmed), but they had no children.

When the emperor was searching for the remains of his father, 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed), an old woman of low status from Ōmi Province came to him and said that she alone knew well where the prince’s remains had been buried, and that they could be identified even by the teeth (a small note says that the teeth were 押歯, divided into three). So people were gathered to dig up the earth, and the remains were found; a tomb was built on the mountain east of 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed) and he was buried there, and the sons of 韓帒 (reading unconfirmed) were made to guard the tomb.

On returning to the capital, the emperor summoned the old woman, praised her for not forgetting the place and keeping it in sight, and gave her the name 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed); he called her into the palace and cared for her generously. He built a dwelling for the old woman beside the palace and summoned her without fail every day, and for summoning her he hung a bell (鐸) at the door of the great hall and rang it. The emperor composed a song about this. Later, when the old woman had grown very old and asked to retire to her home district, the emperor saw her off and composed a song.

He sought out the old boar-keeper (猪甘) who had once taken the two princes’ food while they were fleeing, summoned him to the capital, beheaded him on the bank of the Asuka River (飛鳥河), and cut the tendons of his kinsmen’s knees. It is recorded that for this reason, to this day, his descendants always limp on the days when they go up to Yamato (倭). Because the old man’s whereabouts had been well found out (“志米岐”), that place is called 志米須 (reading unconfirmed).

The emperor deeply hated Emperor 大長谷 (大長谷天皇; reading unconfirmed), who had killed his father, and, wishing to avenge himself on his spirit, was about to send men to destroy his tomb. His elder brother 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed) offered to go himself, and he dug only a little at the side of the tomb and came back. When the emperor asked why he had not destroyed all of it, 意祁命 answered that, although Emperor 大長谷 was their father’s enemy, he was their uncle and also an emperor who had ruled the realm; if they destroyed the whole tomb, later generations would surely condemn them; digging a little was enough to show his shame to later ages. The emperor too acknowledged this as reasonable.

The emperor lived to the age of thirty-eight, ruled the realm for eight years, and his tomb is on 石坏岡 hill at 片岡 (readings unconfirmed). After the emperor’s death, 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed) ruled the realm, residing at the 広高宮 palace at Isonokami (石上) (reading unconfirmed). He married 春日大郎女 (reading unconfirmed), child of Emperor 大長谷若建 (大長谷若建天皇; reading unconfirmed), and 高木郎女, 財郎女, 久須毘郎女, 手白髪郎女, 小長谷若雀命 and 真若王 (readings unconfirmed) were born; and from 糠若子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 丸邇日爪臣 (reading unconfirmed), 春日山田郎女 (reading unconfirmed) was born. His children numbered seven in all, and of them 小長谷若雀命 ruled the realm.

quotes.note: Praising her for not forgetting the place of the remains and keeping it in sight, he gave her the name 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed).
A bell (鐸) was hung at the door of the great hall to summon the old woman.
The words of 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed): Emperor 大長谷 (reading unconfirmed) is our uncle and also an emperor who ruled the realm.
Emperor Kenzō lived to the age of thirty-eight and ruled the realm for eight years.

figures.name: 袁祁之石巣別命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kenzō)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the Near Asuka palace (近飛鳥宮). He searches for and buries his father’s remains, and tries to destroy the tomb of his father’s enemy.

figures.name: 難波王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 石木王 (reading unconfirmed). Wife of Emperor Kenzō; they had no children.

figures.name: 市邊王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of Emperors Kenzō and Ninken. His remains are found at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 置目老媼 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An old woman of Ōmi Province. She reveals where the remains of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed) lie, is given this name, and lives beside the palace.

figures.name: Bell (鐸)
figures.role: The bell hung at the door of the great hall to summon the old woman.

figures.name: The sons of 韓帒 (韓帒之子等; reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: They are made to guard the tomb of 市辺王 (reading unconfirmed) built on the mountain east of 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: The old boar-keeper (猪甘老人)
figures.role: The old man who took the two princes’ food while they were fleeing. He is sought out and beheaded.

figures.name: 大長谷天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The emperor who killed the two princes’ father. His tomb is nearly destroyed.

figures.name: 意祁命, also 意意祁命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ninken)
figures.role: Elder brother of Emperor Kenzō. He remonstrates by only digging a little at the tomb, and after his younger brother’s death rules the realm from the 広高宮 palace at Isonokami (石上) (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 春日大郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor 大長谷若建 (reading unconfirmed). She becomes the wife of Emperor Ninken and bears 小長谷若雀命 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: 小長谷若雀命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Ninken and 春日大郎女 (reading unconfirmed). He ruled the realm next.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, the 1st year of Emperor Kenzō, 2nd month, this month
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, the emperor and the crown prince 億計 (reading unconfirmed), guided by 置目 (reading unconfirmed), dug up the remains at 蚊屋野 in 来田綿, Ōmi (readings unconfirmed), but because they were mixed with the bones of 佐伯部仲子 (reading unconfirmed), an attendant (帳内), the bones of the hands and feet could not be told apart, so two tombs very much alike were built at 蚊屋野. The Kojiki records that the remains could be identified by the teeth, and there is a single tomb.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, the 2nd year of Emperor Kenzō, autumn, 8th month (己未朔)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, when the emperor says he wishes to destroy the tomb of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed) and scatter his bones, the crown prince 億計 (reading unconfirmed) remonstrates with him, giving two reasons, and the emperor says “善哉” (“Well said”) and has the work stopped. There is no story, as in the Kojiki, of the elder brother digging a little at the side of the tomb.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 15, the 3rd year of Emperor Kenzō, summer, 4th month (庚辰)
compare.text: In the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Kenzō dies at the 八釣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) on the day 庚辰 of the 4th month, summer, in the third year after his accession, which differs in the number of years from the Kojiki’s “ruled the realm for eight years” (治天下八歳).

keifu-suiko.title: From Emperor Buretsu to Empress Suiko
keifu-suiko.lead: The ten reigns from Emperor Buretsu to Empress Suiko consist mainly of genealogical entries listing palaces, consorts, children, years of reign and tombs. The narrative entries are limited to two: after the death of Emperor Buretsu, who had no heir, 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor 品太 (品太天皇; reading unconfirmed), was brought from 近淡海国 (reading unconfirmed); and in the reign of Emperor Keitai, 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed) was subdued.

points.text: Emperor Buretsu (小長谷若雀命; reading unconfirmed) had no crown prince, and after his death 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Keitai), a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor 品太 (reading unconfirmed), was brought from 近淡海国 (reading unconfirmed), married to 手白髪命 (reading unconfirmed), and given the realm.
In the reign of Emperor Keitai, because 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed) did not obey the emperor’s commands and was often disrespectful, 物部荒甲之大連 and 大伴之金村連 (readings unconfirmed) were sent and killed 石井.
Of the twenty-five princes and princesses born to Emperor Kinmei, four ruled the realm: 沼名倉太玉敷命 (Bidatsu), 橘之豊日命 (Yōmei), 豊御気炊屋比売命 (Suiko) and 長谷部之若雀命 (Sushun) (readings unconfirmed).
It is recorded that 上宮之厩戸豊聡耳命 (reading unconfirmed) was born to Emperor Yōmei and his half-sister 間人穴太部王 (reading unconfirmed).

The last entry of the Kojiki is Empress Suiko (豊御食炊屋比売命; reading unconfirmed); it records that she ruled the realm for thirty-seven years from the 小治田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and that her tomb, at first on top of 大野岡 hill (reading unconfirmed), was later moved to the great tomb at 科長 (reading unconfirmed).
Emperor Keitai’s age at death differs greatly: forty-three in the Kojiki and eighty-two in the Nihon Shoki.

story.text: 小長谷若雀命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Buretsu) ruled the realm for eight years from the 列木宮 palace at 長谷 (readings unconfirmed). Because he had no crown prince, he established the 小長谷部 (reading unconfirmed) as a group in place of a child (御子代). His tomb is at 石坏岡 hill at 片岡 (readings unconfirmed). When the emperor died there was no prince to take up the succession (日継), so 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor 品太 (品太天皇; reading unconfirmed), was brought up from 近淡海国 (reading unconfirmed), married to 手白髪命 (reading unconfirmed), and given the realm.

袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Keitai) ruled the realm from the 玉穂宮 palace at 伊波礼 (readings unconfirmed). He married 若比売 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 三尾君 (reading unconfirmed) and others; 目子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 凡連 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 尾張連 (reading unconfirmed) and others; and 手白髪命 (reading unconfirmed), child of Emperor 意富祁 (意富祁天皇; reading unconfirmed), as chief consort, among others; his children numbered nineteen in all (seven sons and twelve daughters). Of these, 天国押波流岐広庭命, 広国押建金日命 and 建小広国押楯命 (readings unconfirmed) ruled the realm, and 佐佐宜王 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped at the Ise Shrine. In this reign, because 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed) did not obey the emperor’s commands and was often disrespectful, the two men 物部荒甲之大連 and 大伴之金村連 (readings unconfirmed) were sent and killed 石井. The emperor lived to the age of forty-three, and his tomb is the 藍 tomb at 三嶋 (readings unconfirmed).

広国押建金日命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ankan) ruled the realm from the 金箸宮 palace at 勾 (readings unconfirmed); he had no children, and his tomb is at 高屋村 in 古市, Kawachi (readings unconfirmed). 建小広国押楯命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Senka) ruled the realm from the 廬入野宮 palace at 檜埛 (readings unconfirmed); he married 橘之中比売命 (reading unconfirmed), child of Emperor 意祁 (意祁天皇; reading unconfirmed), and 石比売命, 小石比売命 and 倉之若江王 (readings unconfirmed) were born; and from 川内之若子比売 (reading unconfirmed), 火穂王 and 恵波王 (readings unconfirmed) were born.

Emperor 天国押波流岐広庭 (天国押波流岐広庭天皇; reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kinmei) ruled the realm from the 師木嶋大宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). He married 石比売命 (reading unconfirmed), child of Emperor Senka (in the original text, “檜脾天皇之御子”); her younger sister 小石比売命 (reading unconfirmed); 糠子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 日爪臣 of Kasuga (春日) (reading unconfirmed); 岐多斯比売 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the great minister 宗賀之稲目宿禰 (宗賀之稲目宿禰大臣; reading unconfirmed); and her aunt 小兄比売 (reading unconfirmed); his children numbered twenty-five in all. Of these, four ruled the realm: 沼名倉太玉敷命, 橘之豊日命, 豊御気炊屋比売命 and 長谷部之若雀命 (readings unconfirmed).

沼名倉太玉敷命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Bidatsu) ruled the realm for fourteen years from the 他田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). He married his half-sister 豊御食炊屋比売命 (reading unconfirmed); 小熊子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 伊勢大鹿首 (reading unconfirmed); 比呂比売命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 息長真手王 (reading unconfirmed); and 老女子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 春日中若子 (reading unconfirmed); his children numbered seventeen in all. It is recorded that, of these, the child born to Crown Prince 日子人 (日子人太子; reading unconfirmed) by his half-sister 田村王 (reading unconfirmed; also called 糠代比売命) was the emperor who ruled the realm from the 岡本宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). His tomb is at 科長 in 川内 (readings unconfirmed).

橘豊日命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Yōmei) ruled the realm for three years from the 池辺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed); he married 意富芸多志比売 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the great minister 稲目宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and his half-sister 間人穴太部王 (reading unconfirmed), among others, and from 間人穴太部王 were born 上宮之厩戸豊聡耳命 (reading unconfirmed) and others. His tomb was at 掖上 in 石寸 (readings unconfirmed) and was later moved to the middle tomb at 科長 (reading unconfirmed). Emperor 長谷部若雀 (長谷部若雀天皇; reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sushun) ruled the realm for four years from the 倉椅柴垣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and his tomb is on top of 倉椅岡 hill (reading unconfirmed). 豊御食炊屋比売命 (reading unconfirmed; Empress Suiko) ruled the realm for thirty-seven years from the 小治田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed); her tomb was on top of 大野岡 hill (reading unconfirmed) and was later moved to the great tomb at 科長 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor 品太 (reading unconfirmed), was brought up from 近淡海国 (reading unconfirmed).
竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed) did not obey the emperor’s commands and behaved disrespectfully in many ways.
上宮之厩戸豊聡耳命 (reading unconfirmed) was born to Emperor Yōmei and 間人穴太部王 (reading unconfirmed).
Empress Suiko ruled the realm for thirty-seven years from the 小治田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 小長谷若雀命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Buretsu)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled for eight years from the 列木宮 palace at 長谷 (readings unconfirmed). He had no crown prince and established the 小長谷部 (reading unconfirmed) as a group in place of a child (御子代).

figures.name: 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Keitai)
figures.role: A fifth-generation descendant of Emperor 品太 (reading unconfirmed). He is brought from 近淡海国 (reading unconfirmed) and rules the realm from the 玉穂宮 palace at 伊波礼 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 手白髮命, also 手白髮郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor 意富祁 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ninken). She marries 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed), becomes chief consort, and bears 天国押波流岐広庭命 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He disobeys Emperor Keitai’s commands and is killed by the two men sent against him.

figures.name: 物部荒甲之大連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent together with 大伴之金村連 (reading unconfirmed), he kills 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大伴之金村連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent together with 物部荒甲之大連 (reading unconfirmed), he kills 竺紫君石井 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 佐佐宜王, also 佐佐宜郎女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Keitai. It is recorded that she worshipped at the Ise Shrine.

figures.name: 廣國押建金日命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Ankan)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 金箸宮 palace at 勾 (readings unconfirmed). He had no children.

figures.name: 建小廣國押楯命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Senka)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 廬入野宮 palace at 檜埛 (readings unconfirmed). He had five children.

figures.name: 天國押波流岐廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Kinmei)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled the realm from the 師木嶋大宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). Of his twenty-five children, four rule the realm.

figures.name: 宗賀之稻目宿禰大臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of 岐多斯比売 (reading unconfirmed), consort of Emperor Kinmei, and of 意富芸多志比売 (reading unconfirmed), consort of Emperor Yōmei.

figures.name: 沼名倉太玉敷命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Bidatsu)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled for fourteen years from the 他田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). He had seventeen children.

figures.name: 日子人太子, also 忍坂日子人太子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Bidatsu. It is recorded that his child was the emperor who ruled the realm from the 岡本宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 橘豐日命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Yōmei)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled for three years from the 池辺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). Father of 上宮之厩戸豊聡耳命 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 上宮之厩戶豐聰耳命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Yōmei and 間人穴太部王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 長谷部若雀天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sushun)
figures.role: The emperor who ruled for four years from the 倉椅柴垣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 豐御食炊屋比賣命 (reading unconfirmed; Empress Suiko)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Kinmei and wife of Emperor Bidatsu. She ruled the realm for thirty-seven years from the 小治田宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and is the last sovereign recorded in the Kojiki.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 17, the 25th year of Emperor Keitai, spring, 2nd month (丁未)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives Emperor Keitai’s age as forty-three, but the Nihon Shoki says that he died at the 磐余玉穂宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in the 25th year (the year 辛亥), at the age of eighty-two, and was buried in the 藍野 tomb (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki also notes that “a certain book” (或本) gives a view that he died in the 28th year (甲寅).

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 17, the 22nd year of Emperor Keitai, winter, 11th month (甲寅朔甲子)
compare.text: The Kojiki says that the two men 物部荒甲之大連 and 大伴之金村連 (readings unconfirmed) killed 石井 (reading unconfirmed), but in the Nihon Shoki the great general 物部大連麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) fights 磐井 (reading unconfirmed) in 御井郡 district in Tsukushi (筑紫) (reading unconfirmed) and beheads him, and it also records that his son 筑紫君葛子 (reading unconfirmed) offered the 糟屋屯倉 granary (reading unconfirmed) to escape the death penalty.

compare.where: Nihon Shoki, Book 22, the 36th year of Empress Suiko, autumn, 9th month (己巳朔戊子)
compare.text: The Kojiki places Empress Suiko’s tomb on top of 大野岡 hill (reading unconfirmed) (later moved to the great tomb at 科長), but in the Nihon Shoki the empress left instructions that she was not to be buried lavishly but in the tomb of Prince 竹田 (竹田皇子; reading unconfirmed), and in the 9th month of the 36th year she was buried in Prince 竹田’s tomb accordingly.
